proposals.title: A. Cross-validation hold-out predictions only for held-out rows (gather-decode), skipping the unused full prediction and residual
proposals.location: mixmogam/twostep.py:_hratt_fit_scores (CV fit); mixmogam/_vb.py:VBEngine.fit/_compute_prediction + VBEngine.predict; mixmogam/_loco.py:_decode (+ new row-gather kernels in _standardize.py)
proposals.mechanism: The CV fit (10 grid columns, all holding out fold 0) calls predict(beta) over all n samples, then builds R = Y - prediction and R *= mask (both (n,10) float64). hratt reads only prediction[held] (10% of rows) to compute the MSE. Only `best` (the argmin) feeds the p-values. Proposal: add a private fit keyword, e.g. _prediction_rows=held, and predict(beta, rows=held). Decode just the held rows of each variant slice with a new Numba gather kernel: variant-major int8 reads G[rows[h], j] inside the contiguous column, and two-bit packed reads data[j, i>>2]. A NumPy fallback handles uncompiled storage, and row_scale multiplies by _scale_store[rows]. One float64 GEMM per slice over the same slices as today (lg.slices()) then gives Q[rows] @ (c'beta). This does about 1/10 of the decode writes and GEMM rows, and avoids two (n,P) arrays.
proposals.evidence: Prototype in /tmp/hratt-speed/work/tail/kernels.py (decode_rows_int8/decode_rows_packed, predict_rows_sameslices), driven through a patched _hratt_fit_scores in patch_b.py. Component ABAB, 7 pairs, one thread: wide int8 101->21 ms (median ratio 0.203); tall int8 156->31 ms (0.208); wide packed 164->22 ms (0.137); tall packed 167->20 ms (0.135). Synthetic 50,000 x 4,000 int8 with 5,000 held: 134->20.5 ms (0.150). cv_mse is bit-identical in every check, and so are p-values in whole hratt runs (wide HE/REML, tall HE/REML). Scaling: savings = predict cumtime x (1 - ratio). p3-he 0.842 x 0.79 = 0.66 s; p3-reml 0.825 x 0.79 = 0.65 s; hapnest 0.446 x ~0.82 (between the tall 0.21 and n=50k 0.15 ratios) = 0.37 s.
proposals.memory_effect: Lower. Two fewer (n,10) float64 arrays (prediction and the masked residual; 8 MB at n=50k), and the 16 MiB float64 tile buffer becomes a slice x n_held tile (3.4 MB at p3, 10 MB at n=50k).
proposals.risks: Needs new gather-decode kernels: int8 variant-major, packed, and a NumPy fallback; gwas() always passes variant-major or packed storage. cv_mse stays bit-identical only while the variant slicing matches predict() and Accelerate's DGEMM gives per-row results independent of M. That held in all 6 checks here; otherwise only extra['cv_mse'] would move at 1e-16, not p. tests/test_hratt_crossfit.py monkeypatches VBEngine.predict(self, beta) and counts calls, so it needs updating. Keep `held` in its given (unsorted) order, or the np.mean order changes.
proposals.saving_multicore_note: The gather kernel can be prange'd like decode_table. With 4+ threads the current predict decodes in parallel but its GEMM stays serial, so the absolute saving stays roughly 0.5 s at p3.

proposals.title: B. Out-of-fold LOCO group shares accumulated during the cross-fit sweeps (drops the post-fit genotype pass of _out_of_fold_loco)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py:_refresh_residual (new branch-free variant) + VBEngine.fit (private accumulator keyword); mixmogam/twostep.py:_hratt_fit_scores and _out_of_fold_loco
proposals.mechanism: In the ordinary cross-fit (col_fold = arange(k), no group exclusion) each block's backward GEMM already computes delta = z_block' dbeta for every sample, including each sample's held-out fold column. _refresh_residual then multiplies that entry by zero. The held-out share is exactly what _out_of_fold_loco recomputes with a full float64 genotype pass (5 GEMM columns per sample, 1 used). Proposal: a variant of _refresh_residual that also adds the held-out entry into a per-group (G, n) float64 accumulator own[g]. It is branch-free (hit = 1.0 if fi == col_fold[p] else 0.0; acc += d*hit; d *= 1-hit), so it still vectorizes, and it leaves R, work and change bit-identical. After the fit, prediction = own.sum(0) - own minus the per-fold Q correction from coef = c'beta, which needs no genotype pass. The q x k x G coef comes from _projection and beta.
proposals.evidence: Prototype in /tmp/hratt-speed/work/tail/patch_b.py (_refresh_residual_oof, patched fit, oof_from_own). The kernel microbenchmark (bench_refresh2.py) is cost-neutral: n=5k 26.6 vs 25.0 us/call, 20k 106.5 vs 99.6, 50k 268 vs 254, with R/work/change/own identical to base plus a gather. LOCO fit with and without accumulation, 9 ABAB pairs: median ratio 0.989 (wide) and 0.896 (tall), i.e. no detectable overhead under load average 5-7. The finisher costs about 1% of the old pass: wide 136->1.4 ms, tall 159->2.0 ms, wide packed 150->1.3, tall packed 126->1.8 (7 pairs). Whole-run A+B+D, 6 ABAB pairs, one thread: tall HE 4.750->4.422 s (median ratio 0.950); wide HE 6.095->5.717 s (0.946). Scaling: saving = _out_of_fold_loco cumtime x 0.99: p3-he 0.70, p3-reml 0.72, hapnest-he 0.41, hapnest-reml 0.40 s.
proposals.memory_effect: No growth. The (G,n) float64 accumulator is the same size as today's `own`. Today's `own` already coexisted with the live LOCO engine and Gram cache, because _out_of_fold_loco runs before `del eng`. B removes the pass's 16 MiB tile buffer.
proposals.risks: The scores become the sum of float32 block updates, not an exact float64 recompute from the final beta. The current code deliberately recomputes exactly ('Exact residual from the final effects'), so this is a precision choice for the user. Measured on whole hratt: max|dlog10 p| 1.9e-6 (wide HE), 1.8e-6 (tall HE), 2.6e-6 (tall REML), 7.0e-7 (wide REML). Max relative dchi2 (chi2>1) 1.1e-6; max |dbeta|/se 6.5e-7. lambda_GC 1.446459 -> 1.446458 (tall REML), otherwise unchanged at 6 decimals. Hits at 0.05/m unchanged (29/29 and 186/186). Score error is about 1e-6 of the score SD. Applies only to the default cross-fit; the refit and in-sample paths keep predict. Without Numba, _refresh_residual's NumPy fallback needs the same addition. The test_hratt_crossfit monkeypatches of _out_of_fold_loco keep working if the finisher keeps that name.
proposals.saving_multicore_note: Independent of thread count: a whole genotype pass (parallel decode plus serial float64 GEMM at 4+ threads) disappears, so roughly 0.4-0.6 s at p3 with 4-10 cores, a larger share of a threaded run.

proposals.title: D. chi2(1) tail via erfc(sqrt(x/2)), with scipy's chdtrc kept for the deep tail
proposals.location: mixmogam/twostep.py:_result (p = stats.chi2.sf(chi2, 1))
proposals.mechanism: scipy.stats.chi2.sf(x, 1) goes through chdtrc/igamc at about 0.48 us per value. For one degree of freedom it equals erfc(sqrt(x/2)), a fast vectorized ufunc. Proposal: p = sqrt(0.5*chi2); special.erfc(p, out=p); then for finite chi2 with p <= 1e-280 recompute p with special.chdtrc(1, chi2). That keeps the subnormal range (chi2 about 1280-1425, where plain erfc flushes to 0 earlier) identical to today. NaN and inf map as before. The same helper could serve other df=1 tails.
proposals.evidence: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/tail/sf_test.py: on 400,000 values, chi2.sf 195.6 ms vs erfc 3.0-3.3 ms (7 interleaved reps); chdtrc direct 190 ms, so the cost is the special function, not the wrapper. Accuracy: max|dlog10 p| 1.1e-13 on synthetic chi-square plus extremes up to 2000. On real hratt statistics (check_d.py) max|dlog10 p| is 2.8e-14 (tall) and 1.4e-14 (wide); the NaN and p=0 patterns are identical with the fallback. Scaling: saving = sf time x 0.985: p3 0.192-0.195 s -> 0.19 s; hapnest has 20k variants, ~0.0095 s -> 0.01 s.
proposals.memory_effect: None (in place; no extra m-vector)
proposals.risks: p-values are no longer bit-identical to scipy's igamc; the differences are 1e-13 relative, and scipy's own igamc carries similar error. Any test pinning p against stats.chi2.sf with assert_array_equal would need assert_allclose.

proposals.title: C. Fused decode-and-dot numerator for _retro_stats (Numba, prange over variants)
proposals.location: mixmogam/twostep.py:_retro_stats (non-retrospective branch: num[idx] = Z64 @ Wp[:, g]); new kernel in mixmogam/_standardize.py
proposals.mechanism: Today each slice is decoded to a float64 tile (wide_slices) and multiplied by one residual column with a BLAS GEMV. Proposal: a Numba kernel computes num_j = sum_i lut_j[G_ij] * Wt[g_j, i] directly from int8 or two-bit calls. It uses the comparison select that decode_table already uses, widens the float32 lookup values to float64 (the products equal today's widened ones), and reduces in float64 (reassoc fastmath, or explicit partial sums). No tile is written or re-read, and variants are independent, so prange parallelizes them. The weighted/retrospective branch keeps the tile path, since it needs z rows for zvar and rho.
proposals.evidence: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/tail/retro_kern.py, retro_par.py, retro_par2.py, with base and fused interleaved, 7-9 pairs. One thread: wide 71-78 -> 59-60 ms (ratio 0.78-0.82); tall 80-92 -> 59-63 ms (0.71-0.73). One earlier run at lower machine load gave base 52 vs 53 ms (1.02), so the one-thread gain is load-dependent; the fused kernel was a steady ~59 ms while the BLAS path varied 52-91 ms. A 4-accumulator non-fastmath kernel was slower (1.6x), and a 4-variants-per-pass kernel 1.16x. Four threads, current code (parallel decode, serial GEMV) vs prange kernel: wide 58.5-69.5 -> 19.6-22.5 ms (0.34-0.37); tall 72 -> 23 ms (0.33). Max relative num difference 1e-11 (tiny numerators); max|dlog10 p| 8.5e-14. Scaling at one thread with a ~0.82 ratio: p3 0.56 x 0.18 = 0.10 s; hapnest 0.28 x 0.18 = 0.05 s.
proposals.memory_effect: Lower: no 16 MiB float64 tile. Needs a (G,n) transposed copy of Wp, the same size as Wp (which can then be freed).
proposals.risks: The one-thread gain is uncertain (0-28% across runs under other agents' load), so measure on an idle machine before committing for one thread; the clear win is threaded. Needs int8 and packed kernels, serial and parallel variants (Numba caches per function) and a fallback. Summation order differs from BLAS, so values are rounding-level, not bit-identical.
proposals.saving_multicore_note: Main benefit: with 4 threads, ratio 0.33-0.37 against the current threaded retro pass, about 0.35 s at p3 and 0.18 s at hapnest. More with 10 cores, since the current GEMV stays serial.

proposals.title: E. Strong-structure refit path: per-fold prediction of only the rows each column scores
proposals.location: mixmogam/twostep.py:_hratt_fit_scores (refit=True branch: loco['prediction'][rows, c])
proposals.mechanism: Under strong structure the LOCO fit has k x G columns, and fit() predicts all n samples for every column. The caller then keeps only fold f's rows of column f*G+g, so 80% of the GEMM output is discarded. Proposal: fit with _compute_prediction=False, then for each fold gather-decode that fold's rows (A's kernel) and multiply by that fold's G columns. GEMM work drops k-fold, and the scatter into the (n,G) prediction is the same.
proposals.evidence: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/tail/bench_refit.py, synthetic beta with the real panel layout and 5 folds, 5 ABAB pairs, one thread. Wide (P=100): 483 -> 287 ms (ratio 0.594); tall (P=50): 418 -> 224 ms (0.544). Predictions are bit-identical (max abs diff 0). Not exercised by the four profiles (loco_refit false, lambda 1), so their savings are null. At p3 scale under strong structure this predict would be about 4.8 s, so the saving is about 2 s.
proposals.memory_effect: Lower: no (n, k*G) float64 prediction or residual (e.g. 40 MB at n=50k with k*G=100); per-fold outputs are (n/k, G).
proposals.risks: Depends on A's gather kernel. Bit-identity again relies on DGEMM row/column independence, which held here. Strong-structure path only.

propose:postfit.notes:
My area: HRATT's tail, i.e. everything after the LOCO fit plus the fit's fixed costs. At full scale it costs 2.3 s at p3 (CV predict 0.84 + OOF 0.71 + retro 0.56 + chi2.sf 0.19) and 1.14 s at hapnest (0.45 + 0.41 + 0.28 + 0.01).

**Recommended package:**
- A + D are safe: p-values bit-identical for A, 1e-13 for D.
- B is the largest item. It is the one decision for the user: the cross-fit scores move from an exact float64 recompute to accumulated float32 updates, giving max|dlog10 p| 2.6e-6 and no decision changes.
- A+B+D at full size: about 1.55 s at p3-he (5%), 1.56 s at p3-reml, 0.78 s at hapnest-he (3.4%), 0.77 s at hapnest-reml.
- Whole-run A+B+D on the reduced panels, 6 ABAB pairs: ratio 0.950 (tall HE) and 0.946 (wide HE), measured under load average 5-7 from other agents.

**Not worth doing (measured or argued):**
- **First-touch page faults and large allocations:** about 0.1 ms per MiB. Everything the tail allocates at p3 (m-vectors, the (m,10)/(m,5) betas, three 16 MiB tiles) totals under 15 ms.
- **Re-projection in _retro_stats:** the HRATT residual is already covariate-projected, so project(W) there is redundant, but it costs only about 1 ms (n x G x q).
- **A2, accumulating CV hold-out predictions in the CV sweeps:** a cost argument, not measured. It would remove A's remaining ~0.17 s, but needs an n_held x P gather per block, so the net is about 0. Float32 rounding of the MSE could also flip the grid argmin, which would be an estimator change.
- **Retro pass in float32 (raw_slices + SGEMV):** rejected. It would put float32 error into the final statistic.
- **Removing the retro genotype pass algebraically:** impossible. It needs the final OOF residual; the marginal z'ys part could ride along in prepare_moments, but the score-dependent part cannot.

**Driver audit (computed and discarded):**
- The only discards are the CV full prediction and residual (fixed by A) and the refit path's k-fold redundant prediction (fixed by E).
- structure_test, _he_alpha outputs and REML's 24 passes are all used.
- gwas() adds only the variant_major conversion.

**Interactions with other areas:**
- **B and the sweep proposals:** B adds an argument to _refresh_residual, inside the sweep loop. Anyone rewriting _refresh_residual or the backward GEMM must keep the held-out delta entries available. They are computed today and then zeroed.
- **A and the Gram/fold-layout proposals:** A needs a new row-gather decode in _loco/_standardize, which those proposals could share. For example, a compiled fold gather-and-widen is already on the roadmap.
- **Tests to update:** tests/test_hratt_crossfit.py counts VBEngine.predict(self, beta) calls (A changes the signature) and monkeypatches twostep._out_of_fold_loco (keep that name for B's finisher). Tests pinning p against chi2.sf exactly would need allclose (D).
- **Profile format:** the profiles used read_plink's default int8 decode. Packed calls gave better ratios for A (0.135).
- **Threading:** at 4+ threads the serial GEMM/GEMV in predict, OOF and retro make the tail a larger share. A, B and C (prange) address that.

**Prototypes, all in /tmp/hratt-speed/work/tail/:**
- kernels.py: gather decode, held-row predict, fused retro kernels
- patch_b.py: patched fit with the OOF accumulator, oof_from_own, patched _hratt_fit_scores for A/B
- equiv.py: whole-run equivalence and ABAB timing
- bench_ab.py, bench_bfit.py, bench_refresh2.py, refresh_variants.py: A/B component timings
- retro_kern.py, retro_par.py, retro_par2.py: retro kernels and threading
- bench_refit.py: E
- sf_test.py, check_d.py: D
- bench_a_50k.py: A at n=50k

proposals.title: Joint Gram preparation for HRATT's CV and cross-fit LOCO engines (one gather and one set of fold products), stored as packed triangles without slot 0
proposals.location: mixmogam/twostep.py:_hratt_fit_scores (build both engines before the CV fit); mixmogam/_vb.py:VBEngine._prepare_grams/_gram/_fold_layout (new joint builder) + packed sweep (see packed-storage proposal)
proposals.mechanism: Today the CV engine (10% hold-out) and the LOCO engine (5 folds) each decode every sub-block and build their own Grams. The CV engine widens to float64, runs a full syrk plus a hold-out syrk (110% of the flops) and stores the all-sample slot 0, which the default loco_folds=5 path never reads. The LOCO engine runs NumPy's fancy gather, which comes back F-order and is very slow at large n (8 ms per 128x50k block), widens into a fresh 8*n*k array (page faults), then runs 5 fold syrks. The joint build does one decode and one compiled C-order gather/widen into a reused buffer. It runs the 5 fold syrks H_f; their sum is the all-sample product. One more syrk covers the CV hold-out (10%). The CV training Gram is full - H_cv; the LOCO Grams are full - H_f. Total flops are 110% instead of 210%, with one gather and one decode pass instead of two. Both caches are stored packed and without slot 0, so together they take about 3/4 of the 393 KB per sub-block that the LOCO cache alone takes now, and all 3,140 p3 sub-blocks fit under 1e9: no per-sweep rebuilds.
proposals.evidence: Prototype: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/gram/joint.py (with proto.py packed/drop modes). Micro, both engines per 128-variant sub-block including decode, interleaved over 7 reps (machine load 6-7): n=5,000: current 2.56 ms vs joint 0.97 ms (2.3-2.6x over two sessions); n=50,000: 34.9 vs 11.7 ms (3.0-3.4x) (micro_joint.py). Whole HRATT runs, medians of interleaved pairs: wide HE with gram_cache_bytes=1e8 (emulates p3's partial cache), 6 pairs: Gram time 2.04 -> 0.93 s (2.10x), wall 1.17x. tall HE, 6 pairs: Gram 1.55 -> 0.42 s (3.39x), wall 1.40x. wide REML 1e8, 5 pairs: Gram 2.25x, wall 1.10x. tall REML, 5 pairs: Gram 2.77x, wall 1.13x (t_*.txt). Scaling: the p3 profile gives the current both-engine cost per sub-block (CV 0.65 + LOCO 1.19 + 2 decodes x 0.11 = 2.07 ms) and 2,488 per-sweep rebuilds (2.97 s HE, 3.17 s REML). The joint build costs ~2.07/2.4 = 0.86 ms x 3,140 = 2.7 s, against 5.8 + 2.97 = 8.77 s (HE) and 5.87 + 3.17 = 9.04 s (REML) now. hapnest: 4.6 s of Gram preparation / 3.2 -> 1.4 s. These savings already include those of the packed-storage and compiled-gather proposals; do not add them.
proposals.saving_multicore_note: The remaining build (about 2.7 s at p3, 1.4 s at hapnest) is 5-6 independent syrks per sub-block plus a nogil-capable Numba gather. It could run on a second thread one sub-block ahead of the first CV sweep, or split folds across threads. Unmeasured.
proposals.memory_effect: Lower peak. At p3, both packed caches together hold about 0.65 GB during the CV fit, against about 1.0 GB for the LOCO cache now (CV cache 0.42 GB now). At hapnest 33 MB vs 63 MB. The gather buffer (8*n*128 bytes: 5 MB / 51 MB) replaces today's identical per-call transient and is released after preparation.
proposals.risks: Not bit-identical in principle. The CV engine's all-sample product becomes a sum of fold products, and its all-sample covariate coefficients changed by 1.1e-13 relative; these feed only the choice of the CV grid point. Observed: 0 of 792,576 stored float32 Gram entries differed (wide subset, 7 covariates; eq_joint.py), and p-values were exactly identical in 5 whole-run configurations (wide HE/REML at 1e8, tall HE/REML, wide HE with 5 PCs + 2 noise covariates). Both fold assignments must exist before the CV fit; they do in hratt. Skip the joint path when loco_folds=1 (the later full fit needs slot 0) or when h2j==0. If the budget binds (more than ~620k variants at n=5k), cache the CV slot (33 KB per sub-block) first and the LOCO slots after. Otherwise CV sweeps would start rebuilding where today they don't.

proposals.title: Packed upper-triangle Gram storage plus dropping the unused all-sample slot 0
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py:VBEngine._prepare_grams (budget, slots), VBEngine.fit (slot index, rebuild path), _sweep_column/_sweep_block/_sweep_block_parallel (read packed rows); VBEngine.__init__ flag set by twostep.py:_hratt_fit_scores
proposals.mechanism: The sweep reads only gram[a, a] and gram[a, a+1:], the upper triangle. Storing each slot as row-major packed rows of k(k+1)/2 halves Gram memory. Slot 0 (the all-sample Gram) is stored by both HRATT engines but read by neither when loco_folds>1. Without it, each LOCO sub-block takes 5 packed slots instead of 6 full ones (393 -> 171 KB at q=1). All 3,140 p3 sub-blocks then fit under the 1e9 budget, so the 622 rebuilds per LOCO sweep (2,488 calls, 2.97 s HE / 3.17 s REML) disappear. Each of them is built once instead. The packed kernel takes a row slice view, gram[o - a : o - a + nb], so Numba keeps the unsigned-index vectorization; indexing gram[base + c] directly was 13% slower.
proposals.evidence: Prototype: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/gram/proto.py (sweep_block_packed, prepare_patched, fit_patched). Kernel micro, interleaved over 9 reps (micro_sweep.py): 181.1 vs 182.3 us per 128x10 block, 88.4 vs 91.0 us per 128x5 block; outputs identical. Whole runs: wide HE at 1e8 (emulates p3: 260 of 320 sub-blocks cached, 420 rebuilds over 7 sweeps): the rebuild time 0.91 s went to 0 and p-values were identical. That run used the earlier, slower packing helper, so the measured wall ratio understates the gain. Scaling at p3: LOCO builds fall from 2,518 + 2,488 = 5,006 to 3,140 calls; 1,866 x 1.194 ms (HE) / 1.274 ms (REML), less 622 extra decodes in preparation (0.07 s).
proposals.memory_effect: Lower. p3 LOCO cache goes from ~1.0 GB (budget-bound, partial) to ~0.54 GB (complete); the CV cache from 0.42 to ~0.10 GB.
proposals.risks: The engine must know whether slot 0 will be read. The CV engine reuses it for loco_folds=1, and bolt() reuses the CV engine for its full-data fit. Pass a flag from _hratt_fit_scores, or rebuild when col_fold contains -1. All three sweep variants and the rebuild path must use the packed layout. The warning text and the gram_cache_bytes documentation must count stored slots. Measure Numba vectorization again on other CPUs.

proposals.title: Drop slot 0 only (no kernel change): smaller first step toward packed storage
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py:VBEngine._prepare_grams, VBEngine.fit (gidx offset for the sweep); twostep.py:_hratt_fit_scores flag
proposals.mechanism: Store only the fold slots the fits read (5 for the cross-fit engine, 1 for the CV engine) and shift gidx by one for the sweep. The all-sample Gram is still computed as an intermediate but not kept. With an unchanged 1e9 budget the LOCO cache holds 2,995 instead of 2,518 p3 sub-blocks, so 145 instead of 622 are rebuilt per sweep.
proposals.evidence: Prototype: proto.py drop_full mode; p-values identical (wide HE at 1e8). Saving from budget arithmetic and the profile's per-call rebuild cost: LOCO calls 5,006 -> 2,995 + 4 x 145 = 3,575, so 1,431 x 1.194 ms = 1.71 s (HE) or x 1.274 ms = 1.82 s (REML), minus 0.05 s of extra preparation decodes. Timing in a single noisy run only.
proposals.memory_effect: Lower: the CV cache halves (0.42 -> 0.21 GB at p3); the LOCO cache stays at the budget but covers 19% more sub-blocks.
proposals.risks: Same slot-0 reuse caveat as the packed proposal (loco_folds=1, bolt). Superseded by packed storage, which also removes the remaining 145 rebuilds per sweep.

proposals.title: Compiled fold gather + widening into a reused buffer in _gram (bit-identical)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py:VBEngine._gram (partitioned branch: Zs[:, order].astype(float64); CV branch: Zs.astype(float64) and Z64[:, mask])
proposals.mechanism: NumPy's fancy gather on axis 1 returns an F-order array. It reads 128 rows strided by n for every output column, then astype allocates a fresh 8*n*k array (page faults). A Numba kernel writes the same F-order float64 layout directly from the float32 rows. It works 16 rows (one 128-byte line) at a time, so each row block's reads stay in cache, and fills a buffer reused across sub-blocks. The CV hold-out gather uses the same kernel. The CV widening becomes np.copyto into the reused C-order buffer. Every BLAS call sees the same shapes, layouts and strides, so the results are bit-identical. A C-order gather would be faster still but changes the syrk path (float64 results differ, although the stored float32 values matched in tests).
proposals.evidence: Prototype: proto.py gram_fast + gather_F. np.array_equal Grams and coefficients against _gram on wide and tall, with 7 covariates, for CV, 5-fold and fold-subset calls (eq_fast.py). Micro, both engines per sub-block including decode: 1.27-1.28x at n=5k, 1.30-1.49x at n=50k (micro_joint.py, two sessions). Whole runs: tall HE, 6 pairs: Gram 1.55 -> 0.88 s, wall 1.22x. wide HE at 1e8: Gram 2.04 -> 1.51 s, wall 1.09x; p identical. Scaling alone: p3 8.77 s (HE) / 9.04 s (REML) of Gram work x (1 - 1/1.28); hapnest 4.6 s x (1 - 1/1.35). Combined with packed storage, p3 gains about 1.45 s more. Subsumed by the joint build.
proposals.memory_effect: Peak unchanged: the reused 8*sub_block*n buffer replaces an identical per-call transient. Allocate it in _prepare_grams and in fit only when rebuilds are needed, and release it after.
proposals.risks: Bit-identity depends on matching NumPy's F-order layout; a test should pin the strides. The roadmap's ~0.15 s per engine estimate came from 10k x 30k. At p3 (3,140 sub-blocks plus rebuilds) and n=50k (8 ms gathers) the gain is larger.

proposals.title: Build each sub-block's Grams on first use in the first sweep (no separate decoding pass in _prepare_grams)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py:VBEngine._prepare_grams and VBEngine.fit (sub-block loop)
proposals.mechanism: _prepare_grams decodes every sub-block (raw_slices) only to build Grams. The fit's first sweep then decodes the same rows again for its GEMMs. Cache on first use instead: in sweep 1, when sub-block b is not cached and the budget allows, build its Grams from the rows the sweep just decoded and append them. The rebuild path does this already, minus the append. Same arithmetic, one decoding pass fewer per engine.
proposals.evidence: Profile: _prepare_grams -> raw_slices (decoding) costs 0.644 s at p3 (both engines, 5,661 sub-blocks) and 0.308 s at hapnest. With the joint build only one engine-pass remains, so this saves half (0.32 / 0.15 s). The micro 'joint_nodecode' variant (rows pre-decoded) was within noise of joint at n=5k and 7% faster at n=50k (micro_joint.py). Not prototyped inside fit.
proposals.saving_multicore_note: Also the natural place for the overlap: build sub-block b+1's Grams on a worker thread while sub-block b sweeps.
proposals.memory_effect: None (same cache, filled during sweep 1 instead of before it).
proposals.risks: Grams must exist before a sub-block's first sweep (they do, since they are built just before it). An interrupted fit leaves a partial cache, which is fine. The partial-cache warning must move.

proposals.title: Smaller sub_block (64): halves Gram flops and memory per variant, but the sweeps slow down (measured; not recommended)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py:VBEngine(sub_block=128) as constructed by twostep.py:_hratt_fit_scores
proposals.mechanism: Gram cost and cache size per variant scale with sub_block. At 64 everything fits at p3 even unpacked, and builds are about 1.4x cheaper per variant. In exact arithmetic the Gauss-Seidel iterates do not depend on the block size. But the residual refresh, backward GEMM writes and Python overhead per sub-block double.
proposals.evidence: Micro: both-engine Gram cost per variant 1.36-1.41x lower at n=5k and 1.25-1.48x at 50k (micro_joint.py). Whole runs on wide HE at 1e8: Gram time 2.6x lower, but non-Gram VB time 10% higher (nongram_ratio 0.90 with covariates); wall 1.19x (5 pairs) and 1.09x (1 pair). p changed by up to 2.6e-6 in log10, with no decision changes and lambda_GC unchanged to 6 digits. The p3 estimate is unmeasured at scale: Gram -4.1 s, fit +1.5 s, net ~2.6 s. hapnest is net ~0. After the joint build, the Gram share is too small for this to pay.
proposals.memory_effect: Gram cache per variant halves.
proposals.risks: Not additive with the joint/packed proposals; likely net negative after them. Thinner GEMMs and twice the per-sub-block Python overhead.

proposals.title: Exact integer Gram products in float32 from raw int8 calls, with float64 centering/scaling/covariate corrections (measured; not recommended)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py:VBEngine._gram (would need raw-call access through LocoGenotypes)
proposals.mechanism: Gather the 0/1/2 calls in fold order as float32, run ssyrk per fold (exact while n_f*4 < 2^24), then apply (XX' - mu t' - t mu' + n_f mu mu')/(s s') and the covariate corrections in float64. This needs no widening, and the float32 syrk is about 4x faster than float64 (0.11 vs 0.44 ms at n=5k; 1.16 vs 3.3 ms at 50k).
proposals.evidence: Prototype /tmp/hratt-speed/work/gram/micro_int.py (no missing calls, q=1). Fold-product step: 0.69x (slower) at n=5k, because the per-fold float64 k x k corrections dominate; 1.54x faster at n=50k (13.2 -> 10.6 ms). Applied on top of the joint build: about 0 at p3 and about 160 x 2.6 ms = 0.4 s at hapnest. It changes 32-41% of the stored float32 Gram entries (by one ulp or more; it yields the Gram of the exact standardized values, not of the float32 lookup values the GEMMs use).
proposals.memory_effect: None.
proposals.risks: Real data has missing calls, which add X O' and O O' products (stacked 2k x 2k: 4x the float32 flops, cancelling the gain) or sparse corrections. Covariates other than the intercept need X_f Q_f in float64, which brings the widening back. It does not apply to the weighted path (row-scaled rows) and is only worthwhile at n >= 50k.

proposals.title: Float32 syrk of the decoded float32 rows with an exact float64 diagonal (measured; rejected)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py:VBEngine._gram
proposals.mechanism: Skip the widening and run ssyrk on the float32 rows. The diagonal (which fixes the converged posterior means) is recomputed exactly in float64; the off-diagonal entries only steer the within-block path.
proposals.evidence: Prototype proto.py gram_f32 (micro_compare.py): 0.59-0.89x (slower), because the sequential float64 sums of squares and coefficients in Numba cost more than the saved widening. Off-diagonal error up to 1.1e-5 x sqrt(gii gjj), about 100x the float32 storage rounding.
proposals.memory_effect: None.
proposals.risks: Slower as prototyped and markedly less accurate; not worth pursuing.

propose:gram.notes:
Combined effect: the joint build (with packed storage and no slot 0) plus build-on-first-use would save about 6.4 s at p3-HE (21% of 31.0 s), 6.5 s at p3-REML (11%), 3.35 s at hapnest-HE (15%) and 3.35 s at hapnest-REML (8%). Memory goes down in every case. Not every saving adds up. The joint build already includes the packed-storage, drop-slot-0 and compiled-gather savings. Smaller sub-blocks stop paying once the joint build is in. If the joint build is judged too invasive, the bit-identical package (packed + drop slot 0, compiled gather, build on first use) saves about 4.2 s at p3-HE, 4.4 s at p3-REML and 1.5 s at hapnest.

Equivalence:
- Bit-identical (array-equal Grams and coefficients, identical p-values): packed storage, drop slot 0, compiled gather (eq_fast.py, including 7 covariates).
- Joint build: identical stored float32 Grams (0 of 792,576 entries differ) and identical p-values in 5 whole-run configurations. Only the CV engine's all-sample covariate coefficients differ, by 1.1e-13 relative. Classified as rounding-level for safety.

Measurement caveat: the machine ran at load average 6-7 from other agents. Wall-clock ratios from interleaved pairs are noisy (±10%), so the full-size savings are scaled from component timings (instrumented time in Gram preparation and per-sweep rebuilds, and per-sub-block micro benchmarks) applied to the cProfile splits:
- p3-HE: preparation 5.795 s, of which decoding 0.644 s; rebuilds 2.97 s in 2,488 calls.
- p3-REML: preparation 5.87 s; rebuilds 3.17 s.
- hapnest: preparation 4.6 s, no rebuilds.

The wide panel at gram_cache_bytes=1e8 reproduces p3's partial cache: 260 of 320 sub-blocks cached, against p3's 2,518 of 3,140. It runs 7 LOCO sweeps where p3 runs 4.

Interactions with other areas:
1. Packed storage changes the Numba sweep kernels (_sweep_column and both block wrappers). Any proposal that rewrites the sweep kernel should adopt the packed row read: take a row slice and keep the unsigned loop bounds, or it loses about 13%.
2. The joint build restructures _hratt_fit_scores so both engines exist before the CV fit. Proposals that touch engine lifetime, or that share decoded rows between the CV and LOCO fits, overlap with it.
3. Another proposer (work/vbinner) is also measuring a DROPFULL slot-0 option; merge the two.
4. Build on first use moves Gram building into the fit loop, which conflicts with any fit-loop fusion proposal; coordinate.
5. bolt() and loco_folds=1 reuse the CV engine's slot 0, so the drop must be conditional.

- ab.py: interleaved whole-run A/B with component timers

proposals.title: Gram preparation: decode straight to float64 (fold-sorted for the cross-fit engine); no float32 decode, fancy gather or astype
proposals.area: decoding / data movement (Gram preparation and in-fit Gram rebuilds)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: VBEngine._prepare_grams, VBEngine._gram (fit's rebuild call); new Numba kernel in mixmogam/_standardize.py
proposals.mechanism: Today _prepare_grams decodes float32 sub-blocks through raw_slices. _gram then widens them with Zs.astype(float64) on the CV engine. On the partitioned cross-fit engine it does Zs[:, order].astype(float64): a NumPy fancy gather plus a fresh float64 temporary that page-faults on every call. At p3, 622 of 3,140 sub-blocks are rebuilt on every cross-fit sweep and repeat the gather and widen. The change decodes the int8 calls once per sub-block straight into a reused (sub_block, n) float64 buffer. The CV engine uses the existing decode_table with a float64 output. The cross-fit engine uses a new kernel, out[r,t] = lut[r, G[order[t], idx[r]]], which handles four variants per index load. Rebuilds re-decode from int8 instead of gathering from the float32 rows. The decoded values are identical to today's.
proposals.evidence:
Prototype: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/decode/patches.py ('gram'), kernels.decode_gather4.
Micro-benchmarks (bench_gram2/3/4.py, loaded machine):
- Partitioned path today: 1.6-2.9 ns/call (decode 0.17 + gather 0.7-1.3 + astype 0.6-0.7). Fused: 0.50-0.56 ns/call.
- CV path: decode+astype 0.68-0.94 ns/call; float64 decode 0.23 ns/call.
Paired Gram preparation on the reduced panels (bench_prepare.py, 7 alternating reps):
- wide (n=5000): cross-fit prep 0.572->0.393 s, rebuild 0.620->0.437 s, CV prep 0.373->0.363 s.
- tall (n=20000): cross-fit prep 0.908->0.432 s, rebuild 0.924->0.421 s, CV prep 0.652->0.429 s.
End-to-end ABAB, 6 pairs:
- wide HE 0.899; tall HE 0.811; wide HE with gram_cache_bytes=1e8 (about 20% rebuilt each cross-fit sweep, as at p3) 0.944.
- p-values bit-identical in all three.
Cost included in the estimate: the float64 fold-Gram GEMMs run slower on C-order rows than on the F-order array NumPy's gather returns (0.33->0.43 ms per sub-block at n=5000; 3.75->5.64 ms at n=50000).
Scaling, p3:
- _gram calls from the profile: 3,140 CV prep, 2,518 cross-fit prep, 2,488 rebuilds.
- Per-call savings from wide minus the GEMM penalty, discounted about 35% for machine load (the idle p3 profile shows astype at 0.21 ns/element against about 0.5 under load).
- Cross-check: _gram cum 8.0 s, of which about 2.7 s is float64 GEMM at about 500 GFLOPS, so data movement is about 4.3 s plus 0.64 s prep decode. New data movement is about 2.7 s, giving about 2.0 s.
Scaling, hapnest: 160+160 calls at n=50,000. _gram cum 4.2 s, of which about 1.2 s is GEMM. New cost is about 0.8 s data movement plus 0.3 s GEMM penalty, giving about 1.8 s.
proposals.saving_multicore_note: The kernels are per-variant loops and could take prange workers, as decode_table already does for n_threads > 1.
proposals.memory_effect: Lower or equal. The float32 gathered copy (k*n*4: 2.5 MB at p3, 25.6 MB at hapnest) and the per-call float64 temporary are gone. One persistent (128, n) float64 buffer per engine (5 MB p3, 51 MB hapnest) replaces a temporary of the same size.

- Rounding: the CV-engine Grams are bit-identical. On the cross-fit engine, BLAS rounds F-order and C-order operands differently: 4 of 30.3M stored float32 Gram entries (near-cancelled ones) differed by about 1 ulp on wide (max rel 2.4e-6). p-values stayed bit-identical on all tested runs, but that is not guaranteed.
- Bit-identical fallback: an F-order output kernel (kernels.decode_gather_f) matches today's Z64 bit for bit, including the GEMMs. It runs at 1.1-1.9 ns/call, so it keeps roughly half the saving (about 0.9 s p3, 1.0-1.3 s hapnest).

proposals.title: prepare_moments from exact counts, a centered decode and one BLAS product with Q
proposals.location: mixmogam/_standardize.py: prepare_moments (_moments_tile/_moments_columns_*); LocoGenotypes._prepare
proposals.mechanism:
The current kernel walks 64 variants a sample at a time. Each sample costs 64 strided byte gathers in two passes (counts, then projection with a sequential float64 chain per variant): about 1.7-2 ns/call, 11% of p3-HE.
The change:
- (a) Count calls per variant contiguously with vectorized integer compares. Mean and SD come from the same _count_moments arithmetic, so they are bit-identical.
- (b) Decode centered calls (g - mu, no-calls 0) into a 64 x n float64 tile at decode speed.
- (c) One BLAS product, tile @ Q, gives the covariate coefficients. zz = sumsq/scale^2 minus the c_k^2 in the original order.
proposals.evidence:
Prototype: patches.py ('moments'), kernels.count_calls/decode_centered.
Micro (bench_moments.py, loaded machine), prepare_moments vs new:
- n=5000, q=1: 1.97 -> 0.97 ns/call.
- n=5000, q=11 (covariates): 3.32 -> 1.25.
- n=20000: 2.02 -> 1.00.
- n=50000: 2.09 -> 1.13.
Scaled with these ratios: p3 prepare_moments 3.43 s x 0.51 = 1.75 s; hapnest 1.72 s x 0.46 = 0.79 s. The saving is larger with covariates (2.7x at q=11).
End-to-end equivalence (equiv.py):
- max |dlog10 p|: 8.5e-14 (wide HE), 2.0e-13 (tall HE), 3.6e-14 (wide REML).
- lambda_GC changes in the 15th digit.
- h2, alpha and CV choice identical; no decision changes.
proposals.saving_multicore_note: Tiles are independent: prange over tiles with one single-thread BLAS call each, deterministic for every thread count.
proposals.memory_effect: +64*n float64 tile during LocoGenotypes construction (2.5 MB at p3, 25.6 MB at hapnest). This is inside the existing 64 MiB _STANDARDIZE_WORK_BYTES budget and before any Gram cache exists, so peak memory is unchanged. 16-row tiles would cut it 4x at n >= 50k.
proposals.risks:
- Gives up 'each variant sums its samples in order'. Covariate coefficients differ by up to 1.7e-12 absolute; mean and SD are unchanged.
- Results stay identical across thread counts and int8/packed storage only with fixed 64-variant tiles and identical decoded values.
- The packed path needs a counts kernel; _packed's byte tables already exist.
- The weighted (sq_weights) path needs a second product for wsq; the prototype falls back to the old kernel there.
- The roadmap's bit-identical tiled kernel (1.35-1.4x) is the alternative if rounding-level is not acceptable.
- Overlaps the pre-VB proposer.

proposals.title: CV hold-out predictions accumulated from the sweeps' own updates (drop the CV predict pass)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: VBEngine.fit (small kernel after _refresh_residual, new private flag); mixmogam/twostep.py: _hratt_fit_scores (CV part)
proposals.mechanism: The CV fit's backward GEMM delta = Zs' changes already covers all n samples; only the residual update zeroes the held-out rows. A Numba kernel adds the held-out rows of delta (n_held x P) to a float64 accumulator after each block. The held-out prediction is then acc - Q[held] @ A, where A = c'beta is already tracked by the fit. The CV fit runs with _compute_prediction=False. That removes VBEngine.predict, a float64 decode plus float64 GEMM over all m variants for 10 columns of which only 10% of the rows are used, and the (n, P) prediction and resid arrays.
proposals.evidence:
Prototype: patches.py ('acc_cv'), _acc_cv kernel.
Component timing (bench_acc_component.py, 7 alternating pairs):
- wide CV fit + MSE: 1.336 -> 1.243 s. The difference equals the predict pass alone (0.104 s).
- tall: 1.479 -> 1.258 s.
Accumulation overhead (bench_acc_kernels.py): 2.5 us/block at n=5000, 33 us/block at n=50000.
Scaled: the profile's predict cost minus overhead.
- p3: 0.842 s - 3,140x5x2.5 us = 0.80 s.
- hapnest: 0.446 s - 162x12x33 us = 0.39 s.
End-to-end: cv_mse relative change 2.1e-8 (wide) and 1.3e-8 (tall); the chosen grid point is unchanged, so p-values are bit-identical on both panels.
proposals.memory_effect: Lower. n_held x P float64 (40 KB at p3) replaces the (n, P) prediction and resid arrays plus the 16 MiB predict tile buffer. predict ran while the CV Gram cache was still alive, so this also lowers that phase's peak.
proposals.risks:
- extra['cv_mse'] changes at the 1e-8 level: the predictions come from the float32-rounded applied changes, not an exact float64 recomputation.
- An exact-tie argmin could in principle flip the chosen grid point; p-values were otherwise bit-identical.
- Exact alternative: a gather-decode of held-out samples only, with a 10x smaller float64 GEMM. Unmeasured; about 0.6-0.7 s at p3.

proposals.title: Out-of-fold LOCO predictions accumulated in the cross-fit sweeps (drop _out_of_fold_loco)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: VBEngine.fit (private flag + small kernel); mixmogam/twostep.py: _hratt_fit_scores, _out_of_fold_loco
proposals.mechanism:
In the ordinary cross-fit, column f is fold f's fit and its held-out rows are fold f's samples. The backward GEMM already gives delta[i, folds[i]], each sample's change under its own out-of-fold fit. Two accumulators are added:
- acc[g_block, i] += delta[i, folds[i]] per block, as one gather-add of n values.
- coef_g[f, :, g_block] += (c' changes)[:, f], from the e = coef.T @ d64 the fit already computes.
These are exactly the own and coef arrays _out_of_fold_loco builds. The same 'total - own' and covariate formula is then applied. This removes one float64 decode plus (n x k) GEMM pass over all variants, in which 4/5 of the GEMM output is discarded.
proposals.evidence:
Prototype: patches.py ('acc_oof'), _acc_oof kernel.
Component timing (7 pairs): wide cross-fit fit + OOF 0.876 -> 0.764 s (OOF pass alone 0.099 s); tall 1.030 -> 0.831 s.
Overhead: 4.4 + 1.7 us/block at n=5000; 40.6 + 1.9 us/block at n=50000. An earlier version that branched inside _refresh_residual doubled its cost; the separate kernel avoids that.
Scaled from the profile's OOF cost minus overhead:
- p3: 0.705 / 0.731 s minus 3,140x4x6.1 us = 0.62 / 0.65 s.
- hapnest: 0.412 / 0.409 s minus 162x8x42.5 us = 0.36 / 0.35 s.
End-to-end:
- OOF predictions differ by up to 3.9e-7 relative.
- max |dlog10 p|: 1.9e-6 (wide HE), 1.8e-6 (tall HE), 7.0e-7 (wide REML), 2.6e-6 (tall REML).
- lambda_GC: 1.0818242 -> 1.0818236 (wide); 1.4450306 -> 1.4450309 (tall).
- No decision changes at 0.05/m.
proposals.memory_effect: Neutral to lower. A (G, n) float64 accumulator (0.8 MB p3, 2.4 MB hapnest), the same size as _out_of_fold_loco's own, is allocated during the fit instead of after it. The 16 MiB tile buffer is gone, and _out_of_fold_loco no longer runs while the cross-fit Gram cache (about 1 GB at p3) is alive.
proposals.risks:
- Rounding-level change: scores come from float32-rounded applied changes and float32 GEMM rather than an exact float64 recomputation from the final beta.
- The binary path's logistic offsets (keep_prediction) inherit the same 1e-7 change.
- Exact fallback: one GEMV per fold on fold-gathered samples instead of a k-column GEMM. It removes only the wasted 4/5 of the OOF GEMM; unmeasured, about 0.2 s at p3.
- The same accumulation would also remove the (k x G)-column predict under strong-structure refit (not profiled here).

proposals.location: mixmogam/_loco.py: LocoGenotypes._products (total += contrib; own[...] += ...); mixmogam/twostep.py: _he_alpha (KP[a] += prod[:, :c]; cross[a] += prod[:, c:])

propose:decode.notes:
Decoding passes. Counted by instrumenting decode_table (count_passes.py) on the reduced panels and from profile call counts at full size.

| run | total passes | HE | Gram prep | CV sweeps | CV predict (f64) | cross-fit sweeps | OOF (f64) | retro (f64) | SLQ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| p3-HE | 14.8 | 1 | 1.8 | 5 | 1 | 4 | 1 | 1 | – |
| p3-REML | 38.8 | 1 | 1.8 | 5 | 1 | 4 | 1 | 1 | 24 |
| hapnest-HE | 27 | 1 | 2 | 12 | 1 | 8 | 1 | 1 | – |
| hapnest-REML | 51 | 1 | 2 | 12 | 1 | 8 | 1 | 1 | 24 |

- p3 also has about 3.2 passes' worth of Gram-rebuild gather/widen from rows already decoded, plus one prepare_moments pass.
- The reduced panels converge more slowly: wide 13+7 sweeps, tall 7+6.
- Decode runs at 0.154-0.176 ns/call at every stage, i.e. at its floor. It is write-bound on the float32 operand, so a decoded cache gains nothing unless it holds all of the panel (8 GB at p3, 4 GB at hapnest); a partial cache trades about 1 GB for under 25% of one sweep's decode.
- The two accumulation proposals bring the passes to 12.8 / 36.8 / 25 / 49.

Rejected or not proposed:
1. Fusing retro with OOF is impossible: every group's residual needs the complete out-of-fold prediction. With OOF accumulation only the retro pass remains.
2. A shared decode for the CV and cross-fit Gram preparation would keep both caches alive (+0.4 GB at p3).
3. Warm-starting the cross-fit from the CV beta would cut sweeps, but it leaks held-out-fold information into out-of-fold scores.
4. Fusing CV Gram preparation into the HE pass saves at most one int8 read.

Negative result (multicore). I prefetched the next slice/sub-block on a helper thread with a nogil copy of the decode kernel (patches.py 'prefetch'). p-values were bit-identical, but it ran 1.19x slower on wide HE, 1.06x slower on wide REML and 1.02x slower on tall HE. One handoff per 128-row sub-block contends for the GIL with the non-nogil Numba sweep kernels, and the extra thread competed on a loaded machine. Overlap needs chunked handoffs, nogil sweeps and an idle machine to judge; that is for the multicore proposer.

Interactions:
- gram overlaps the gram/budget proposers; moments overlaps pre-VB; acc_cv/acc_oof overlap the tail/vbinner proposers.
- Anyone touching _gram should know that NumPy's Zs[:, order] returns an F-order array. The float64 fold Grams depend on that layout for both speed (C-order is 1.3-1.5x slower) and rounding.

All five together (gram, acc_cv + acc_oof, moments, accum), end-to-end ABAB on a loaded machine (load average 5.5-7):
- wide HE 0.941, tall HE 0.735, wide REML 0.982, tall REML 0.827.
- max |dlog10 p| 2.6e-6; no 0.05/m decisions changed; h2, alpha and CV choice identical.
- Projected full-size savings: p3-HE about 5.2 s (17%), p3-REML about 5.65 s (10%), hapnest-HE about 3.5 s (15%), hapnest-REML about 4.3 s (10%).

Measurement caveats:
- Six to eight benchmark processes ran concurrently on 6 P-cores. End-to-end ratios vary about ±10% pair to pair; for example acc_cv alone read 0.92 in one run and 1.02 in the next.
- Savings were therefore taken from paired component timings scaled by the idle full-size profiles' call counts and costs.
