proposals.title: Column-major (P, n) residual, GEMM image and update, with a four-column refresh kernel
proposals.area: VB inner loop: GEMMs + residual refresh
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: VBEngine.fit (R/work/delta/products/changes allocation, forward and backward np.matmul, s_proj), _refresh_residual; _GemmWorkspace (threaded n>=50k path)
proposals.mechanism: Store R (float64), work (storage-precision image) and delta as (P, n) C-order arrays instead of (n, P). Forward becomes products^T = work @ Zs.T into a flat (P, k) buffer, backward becomes delta = changes^T @ Zs. Accelerate runs both orientations much faster: the (n, P) output with leading dimension 5 or 10 is the slow case. The refresh kernel then walks four columns at a time over contiguous sample streams. Each column's squared change is still summed over samples in order, so the sums are bit-identical, but the four independent chains are about 2x faster than the current i-outer/p-inner loop. Two things keep this bit-identical. (a) s_proj = Q' R is computed once per sweep from a sample-major copy, np.ascontiguousarray(R.T), because the q=1 gemv picks a different kernel on the transposed operand. (b) A tail sub-block (k < 128) is multiplied as the whole 128-row decode buffer and the first k outputs are kept, because Accelerate's k-row sgemm differs from the 128-row one only in this orientation. Also: d64 = changes.astype(float64, order='C') keeps the q>1 BLAS inputs in their current layout, and the decode buffer should be zero-initialized so stale tail rows are finite. The threaded path's per-sub-block np.copyto into F-order scratch is no longer needed.
proposals.evidence: Instrumented fit, wide HE n=5,000, per sub-block: P10 sweep 162 us, forward GEMM 89, backward 44, refresh 40, q-corrections 22, gather/scatter 6. P5: 86/88/41/24/80/6. This model reproduces the p3 fit tottime (9.8 s modelled vs 10.1 s profiled). Micro-benchmarks (gemm_micro.py, refresh_micro2.py; refresh bit-identity asserted): n=5,000: backward 44->22 us, forward 92->88. n=20,000: forward 410->270, backward 138->95. n=50,000: forward 2.2->1.04 ms, backward 1.03->0.76 ms. Refresh with folds: n=5,000 P10 43.5->22.0 us, P5 25.4->13.9; n=50,000 P10 441->216, P5 263->132. Interleaved fit-only timing (fitab.py, 7 ABAB pairs, wide): CV fit ratio 0.958 (-26 us per sub-block), LOCO 0.927 (-39 us per sub-block). Combined with the next two items: wide 0.84/0.74, tall (n=20k) 0.76/0.66, synthetic n=50k 0.79/0.74. p-values and betas bit-identical end to end on wide and tall, HE and REML, with q=1 and q=5. Scaling: p3 = 15,700 P10 + 12,560 P5 sub-block visits (HE; REML has 4 CV sweeps) x 26-40 us -> ~0.9 s. hapnest = 1,920 P10 + 1,280 P5 visits x ~1.3-1.4 ms; the model is calibrated to the profiled 9.8 s fit tottime and cross-checked against the syn50k fit-time ratios (3.1-4.3 s range). Prototype: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/vbinner/proto_fit.py (LAYOUT=1); results in fitab.jsonl and results_all.jsonl.
proposals.memory_effect: Same arrays, transposed. Adds one (n, P) float64 transient per sweep for s_proj (0.4 MB at p3, 4 MB at n=50k, P=10). Removes the threaded path's per-sub-block F-order scratch copy.
proposals.risks: Bit-identity depends on Accelerate giving identical results for the two GEMM orientations and for padded tails. This was verified at n=5k/20k/50k and in full fits, but OpenBLAS/MKL (Linux CI) may differ at rounding level. raw_slices must expose its 128-row buffer, or the engine must own it. The threaded n>=50k backward split must cut over output columns instead of rows (tested bit-identical).

proposals.title: Rank-q covariate corrections in two Numba kernels for all columns
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: VBEngine.fit (the per-column-set loops before the sweep and after _refresh_residual)
proposals.mechanism: The per-sub-block loops over column sets are replaced by two kernels. One adds T_g A - c(s_proj + train_g A) to U, with T_g = coefs[0] - coefs[g]. The other subtracts W from s_proj, adds the two quadratic terms to change, and adds e to A. W = T_g' d is computed by a sequential Numba dot, and e = c' d stays one BLAS call. train becomes a (slots, q, q) array indexed by gidx. This replaces about 10 NumPy calls per column set: 1 set in the CV fit, 5 in the cross-fitted LOCO fit. That is p3's 157,010 einsum calls plus about 4x as many small matmuls and fancy-index copies.
proposals.evidence: Instrumented q-correction cost: 22 us per P10 sub-block, 80 us per P5 (cross-fit) sub-block. fitab.py, 7 interleaved pairs on wide (QFUSE only): LOCO fit ratio 0.868 (-80 us per sub-block), CV 0.988 (-7 us). End to end: p and beta bit-identical with q=1 (wide and tall, HE and REML). With 4 covariates (q=5): max |dlog10 p| 2.1e-14 (wide) and 2.8e-14 (tall); lambda_GC equal to 15 digits; no change in 0.05/m decisions. Scaling: p3-HE 12,560 LOCO visits x 80 us + 15,700 CV x 7 us = 1.1 s; REML 1.09 s. hapnest 1,280 x 80 us + 1,920 x 7 us = 0.12 s. Prototype: proto_fit.py (QFUSE=numba; QFUSE=stack keeps W in NumPy).
proposals.memory_effect: Negligible: q x P scratch and a (slots, q, q) train array
proposals.risks: Bit-identical only for q=1, where every sum over q is a single product. With covariates, the q-sum order differs from BLAS, giving a measured 1e-14-level change. The saving grows with q because the current per-set BLAS calls do more work.

proposals.title: Cache only the Gram slots a fit reads (drop the unused full-data slot)
proposals.area: VB Gram cache (interacts with the Gram area)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: VBEngine._prepare_grams (storage) and fit (two gidx maps: stored Grams vs coefs)
proposals.mechanism: Both HRATT engines use only the held-out-fold slots. The CV engine uses gidx=1 for all columns; the cross-fit engine uses 1..5. Yet every cached sub-block stores G[0], the full-data Gram, as well: half the CV engine's cache and 1/6 of the LOCO engine's. Store G[slots used] only, while still computing full as the base. Keep coefs for every slot, since coefs[0] is needed for T. Then, under the same 1e9-byte budget, the p3 LOCO engine caches about 3,010 of 3,140 sub-blocks instead of 2,518. That removes about 490 _gram recomputes per LOCO sweep. Recomputed sub-blocks still index the full _gram output.
proposals.evidence: proto_fit.py DROPFULL=1, ab.py whole GWAS on wide. gram_cache_bytes was set to 102.2e6 to reproduce p3's 80% LOCO cache fraction (256 of 320 sub-blocks), which becomes 96% with dropping. 5 pairs: VB fit time saved 0.32 s (ratio 0.94), about 0.93 ms per avoided recompute. p and beta bit-identical, HE and REML. Scaling: p3 has 4 LOCO sweeps x ~492 fewer recomputes x 0.93 ms = 1.8 s (both HE and REML, 4 LOCO sweeps each). hapnest is fully cached, so no time saving.
proposals.memory_effect: Same budget, used for more sub-blocks. Lowers the CV engine's Gram memory by half (about -205 MB at p3 during the CV fit) and the LOCO engine's by 1/6 when it is fully cached.
proposals.risks: Engines reused for a fit that reads slot 0 must keep it: bolt() reuses its CV engine for col_fold=-1 LOCO, and so does HRATT with loco_folds=1. Add a constructor flag such as keep_full (default True, False for HRATT's CV and cross-fit engines), or rebuild on demand. Overlaps with Gram-area proposals (the budget, recompute costs).

proposals.title: Contiguous variant ranges as views (no beta/scale/projection gather and scatter)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: VBEngine.fit (bb = ascontiguousarray(beta[idx]), scale[idx], _projection[idx], beta[idx] = bb)
proposals.mechanism: Block indices are consecutive whenever variants are sorted by chromosome (the usual case). When idx[-1]-idx[0] == k-1, use beta[s:e], scale[s:e] and _projection[s:e] as C-contiguous views. The sweep then updates beta in place, with no gather or scatter. Convert scale with ascontiguousarray once per fit, not per sub-block. Fall back to the copies for non-contiguous idx.
proposals.evidence: The instrumented gather plus scatter was 6 us per sub-block (n-independent). fitab.py (SLICES only, 7 pairs on wide): CV -6 us, LOCO -4 us per sub-block, ratio 0.99, which is close to the +-4% null-control noise. Bit-identical. Scaled: 28,260 (p3-HE) and 25,120 (p3-REML) visits x 5 us; hapnest 3,200 x 5 us.
proposals.memory_effect: Removes two small (k x P) copies per sub-block
proposals.risks: None beyond keeping the copy path for unsorted inputs

proposals.title: Elastic-net posterior mean with fewer transcendentals (rounding-level)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: _pm_enet, _ndtr_parts (used by _sweep_column)
proposals.mechanism: Same formula, computed with log z = x^2/2 + log Phi(x). The inverse Mills ratios become exp(-log z)/sqrt(2 pi), each mixture uses one exp of the smaller weight plus log1p instead of two exps and a log, and log(0.5 lam) + 0.5 log(2 pi / a) + 0.5 log(v t) merge into one log. The count drops from 2 erfc + 8 log + 6 exp to 2 erfc + 3 log + 3 exp + 1 log1p. erfc (about 18 ns each, 36 ns of the 105-130 ns per evaluation) remains the floor.
proposals.evidence: The posterior mean is 70% of the sweep: pm-only 123 us of 178 us per P10 sub-block, about 96-127 ns per evaluation. pm_check.py: 126-130 -> 105-108 ns per evaluation; sweep kernel on captured sub-blocks 178->163 us (P10) and 92->86 us (P5), -8%. Relative pm differences are median 1e-14; the largest, 4e-5, occur only where the posterior mean nearly cancels to 0. End to end: wide max |dlog10 p| 1.8e-7, tall 8.5e-14; lambda_GC 1.0818242 vs 1.0818241; same 0.05/m hits and same iteration counts. Scaled: p3 sweep 3.6 s x 8%; hapnest 3.3M evaluations x 15 ns. Prototype: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/vbinner/pm_fast.py.
proposals.memory_effect: None
proposals.risks: Changes rounding of every effect, so it is only worth bundling with a deliberate numerics change. The roadmap already declined a log-hoisting rewrite for this reason. The asymptotic x<=-20 branch must be kept as written (the prototype keeps it).

proposals.title: Bit-identical sweep micro-optimizations (hoisted log p, skipped exp(0), paired SNPs or columns)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: _sweep_column, _pm_enet
proposals.mechanism: Three variants: pass log(p) and log(1-p) per column; return 1.0 instead of exp(0) for the maximal weight; apply the Gram corrections of two consecutive SNPs in one pass; advance two columns together for instruction-level parallelism. All keep every operation and its order.
proposals.evidence: sweep_proto.py on 80 captured sub-blocks per P, all bit-identical (U, beta, D): orig 175.7 / 93.5 us; hoisted-only 170.4 / 91.4; 2-SNP 170.9 / 90.8; column pairs 169.6 / 92.1 (P10 / P5). That is 2-3%. The posterior mean is throughput-bound (120 ns independent vs 143 ns chained). The Gram-update loop is already 16-wide vectorized (fcvtl/fmul.2d in the assembly).
proposals.memory_effect: None
proposals.risks: Marginal gain for added kernel complexity; probably not worth doing on its own

proposals.title: CV fit: predict only the held-out rows
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: VBEngine.fit (_compute_prediction) / predict; twostep._hratt_fit_scores uses only cv['prediction'][held]
proposals.mechanism: Accumulate z[:, held_in_tile].T @ bb per decoded tile instead of all samples, and skip resid.
proposals.evidence: predict_rows.py: bit-identical. Wide predict 83.9 -> 75.5 ms (0.90); tall 116 -> 130 ms (no gain). Decoding the float64 tiles dominates, and the gather costs what the smaller GEMM saves. Scaled: at most 10% of p3's 0.84 s predict.
proposals.memory_effect: Smaller (n_held x P) outputs
proposals.risks: Not worth an API change; listed to close the question

proposals.title: Fold the q-correction kernels into the sweep and refresh calls
proposals.area: VB inner loop: Numba dispatch overhead
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: VBEngine.fit (after the two items above)
proposals.mechanism: With the column-major layout and the fused covariate kernels, each sub-block still makes about 13 Python-level calls. Two merges are possible: cov_forward into the sweep kernel, and W/e/cov_backward into the refresh kernel. Each removes one or two Numba dispatches with 8-10 array arguments, at about 1.5-2 us each.
proposals.evidence: Not measured. Estimate: 3 dispatches x ~1.5 us x 28,260 visits at p3.
proposals.memory_effect: None
proposals.risks: Larger kernels; only worth it after the main items land

propose:sweep.notes:
The bit-identical items combined (column-major layout, fused q-corrections, slices, used-slot Gram cache) were measured as whole GWAS, 6 interleaved pairs, under machine load around 6.5. Wide HE with p3-like cache pressure: total ratio 0.865, VB fit ratio 0.806. Tall HE: 0.83 and 0.77. p and beta were bit-identical in every q=1 run (wide and tall, HE and REML). With 4 covariates the only difference comes from the fused q-corrections (max |dlog10 p| 2.8e-14). By the component model this is about 4.0 s at p3-HE (13%), 3.9 s at p3-REML, about 3.6 s at hapnest-HE and 4.0 s at hapnest-REML. Absolute times on this loaded machine run 1.3-2.5x slower than idle, worst for the bandwidth-bound n=50k GEMMs. Use the per-pair ratios and the per-sub-block savings above, not raw seconds.

Interactions:
(1) The used-slot Gram cache overlaps the Gram area: the same 1e9 budget, fewer per-sweep recomputes. It adds to any change that makes _gram itself cheaper, and needs a keep_full flag because bolt() and loco_folds=1 reuse the engine with col_fold=-1.
(2) The column-major layout needs the decode buffer exposed by raw_slices (for padded tails) and should zero-initialize it. With a sample-major decode, the forward GEMM would be 4x faster but the backward 4-6x slower (gemm_micro2/3.py), so I don't recommend changing the decode layout.
(3) The threaded n>=50k path (_GemmWorkspace) already copies work to F order for speed. The layout makes that copy unnecessary; its backward split must cut output columns instead of rows (split_gemm.py: bit-identical).

Multi-core: splitting either GEMM over 4 threads is bit-identical but slower at n=5k (AMX is shared per cluster) and helps only the n=50k backward. The refresh kernel's four-column groups could use prange bit-identically (about 0.3 s at p3 or hapnest with 3+ threads, not measured). Overlapping decode of the next sub-block with the current sweep would need nogil decode kernels and a second buffer (+2.6 MB at p3, +25.6 MB at hapnest), up to about 3.7 s at p3 (not measured).

Rejected after measurement or analysis:
- 64-row sub-blocks: rounding-level (dlog10p 2.6e-6), not faster on wide (0.872 vs 0.865 total). The halved Gram cost is offset by per-block refresh, Python and forward-GEMM overheads.
- 256-row sub-blocks: Gram memory and compute double.
- float32 residual or refresh fused into the GEMM via beta=1: about 1e-5 relative drift, comparable to tol, and it breaks fold masks.
- Freezing converged columns: changes the estimator.

Prototypes and harnesses are in /tmp/hratt-speed/work/vbinner/:
- proto_fit.py: flags LAYOUT, QFUSE, SLICES, DROPFULL, SUBBLOCK, SWEEP.
- ab.py: whole-GWAS ABAB, p/beta/lambda_GC comparison.
- fitab.py: fit-only interleaved timing on captured calls, plus a synthetic n=50k panel under 900 MB RSS.
- fit_instr.py and run_instr.py: component split.
- Micro-benchmarks: gemm_micro*.py, refresh_micro*.py, sweep_proto.py, pm_fast.py, pm_check.py.
- Results: results_all.jsonl and fitab.jsonl.

One run exceeded the memory rule: the first synthetic 50k generator reached 1.75 GB RSS. It was fixed to chunked generation (869 MB).

proposals.title: Stop the REML Lanczos run once h2 has converged (adaptive passes, still capped at 24)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_slq.py:lanczos_quadrature_batch; mixmogam/lmm.py:LMM._slq_pack/_fit_variance_components; mixmogam/twostep.py:fit_variance_components
proposals.mechanism: Each Lanczos step is one full pass over the genotypes (decode plus two GEMMs). The rules after j steps are exactly what a j-step run would return, because Lanczos is incremental. After each step from j = 6 on, the change rebuilds the j-step rules and recomputes REML h2 (the 101-point delta grid plus brentq). It stops after at least 8 steps once two consecutive h2 changes are below 1e-6. slq_steps=24 becomes a maximum. In the n << m regime (P3) the spectrum is narrow and h2 converges in 8-9 passes. At n/m = 2-2.5 (HAPNEST-like) it takes 14-15 passes. Same probes, same quadrature, same delta search; only truncation error below 1e-6 is given up.
proposals.evidence: Prototype: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/pre-vb/adaptive_lanczos.py. The oracle in adaptive_steps.py evaluates h2 from the truncated rules of one 24-step streaming run. Truncation error against 24 steps: on wide (n/m 0.125) 6 steps 3e-6, 8 steps 1.3e-8, 12 steps 2e-13; on wide 1000x40000 (n/m 0.025) 8 steps 2.6e-11; on the full tall panel (n/m 2) 12 steps 8.5e-7, 16 steps 2.9e-9; on a HAPNEST subset (12,500 x 5,000 from the n=50k BED, n/m 2.5) 14 steps 3.4e-7. Monte Carlo SD of h2 over probe seeds (48 probes) is 2e-3 to 6e-3, so the stopping error is about 1e-4 of the MC error. A corrected dense steps study also gives 24 vs 64 steps within 7e-7 at n/m 2.5 and 3e-15 at n/m 0.125. In-process ABAB, REML only: wide stops at 9 passes, ratio 0.393, saves 2.58 s; tall stops at 14 passes, ratio 0.607, saves 2.22 s; HAPNEST subset stops at 15 passes, ratio 0.81 (small problem where check overhead matters). Complete gwas() on wide, 5 ABAB pairs: ratio 0.728, saves 2.67 s per fit. Equivalence on complete gwas(): wide max |dlog10 p| 1.5e-6, tall 5.1e-6, lambda_GC changes by at most 1e-6, 0 of 29 / 186 decisions at 0.05/m changed, same CV choice and LOCO iterations. Each check costs about 31 ms in the prototype. Scaling uses the profiles' per-pass costs: P3 26.9 s / 24 = 1.12 s per pass, 15-16 passes saved, minus about 0.1 s of checks, so about 17 s. HAPNEST 19.1 s / 24 = 0.8 s per pass, 9-10 passes saved (from the HAPNEST subset and tall), minus about 0.35 s of checks, so about 7 s.
proposals.memory_effect: None added. Fewer Krylov slices are written (the np.empty basis is touched only up to the stopping step), so the touched basis shrinks by about 40% at HAPNEST (about 190 of 470 MB).
proposals.risks: This changes a numerical default: slq_steps becomes a cap, and a tolerance parameter is needed (0 restores the fixed 24 steps exactly). It belongs in the CHANGELOG. The prototype replicates REML only without deflation. Production should run the check through _slq_pack's own closures so the deflated case (strong structure), ML and alpha_method='reml' are covered. A temporary stall in convergence could stop early; the observed worst error was 3.4e-7 in h2, and requiring 2-3 consecutive small changes and at least 8 steps guards against it. The check should be vectorized over rules (about 31 ms now) so it stays negligible on small problems. Other callers of LMM.fit(solver='slq') (bolt-inf) would inherit it.

proposals.title: HE alpha pass: one backward GEMM over all five alphas in sample tiles, plus one contiguous accumulator
proposals.location: mixmogam/twostep.py:_he_alpha
proposals.mechanism: Each slice currently runs five backward GEMMs Z' (T * w_a) of width c+q (34), then 2A strided float64 adds. The weighted products are now stacked (k, A, c+q) and one GEMM of width A(c+q) = 170 runs per sample tile. The tile has n/A samples, so the product buffer is the same size as today's n x (c+q) buffer. KP and cross live in one (n, A, c+q) float64 array, so each tile is a single contiguous add; KP and cross become strided views of it, so the rest of the function is unchanged. AMX GEMM cost is nearly flat in output width in this regime, so one 170-wide GEMM costs 0.44-0.61 of five 34-wide ones.
proposals.evidence: Prototype: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/pre-vb/he_stacked.py (install2). GEMM microbenchmark (gemm rates in he_gemm_rate.py): five 34-wide GEMMs against one 170-wide GEMM (2048-sample tiles) gave 0.56 at n=5000, 0.58 at 20,000 and 0.52 at 50,000. Breakdown of the current pass: backward GEMMs about 50% of _he_alpha, diagonal 15-20%, KP adds 5-11%. In-process ABAB of _he_alpha, 9 pairs: wide ratio 0.805, tall 0.828. Scores, h2_HE and alpha were bit-identical, and complete-gwas p-values on wide (HE) were bit-identical. Scaled by the profiles' _he_alpha cumulative times (P3 2.8 s, HAPNEST 2.2 s HE / 2.0 s REML) times 0.18.
proposals.memory_effect: Neutral. The tile buffer equals today's n x (c+q) float32 product buffer, the stacked weighted products add k x 170 float32 (under 0.6 MB), and the combined accumulator is the same bytes as KP plus cross.
proposals.risks: Bit-identity depends on Accelerate computing each output column independently of output width. It held on both panels, but tests should pin it. On another BLAS it could become rounding-level.

proposals.title: Dense float32 kinship for the REML passes when n is small (e.g. n <= ~8,000 and n^2*4 <= the VB Gram cache the run will hold)
proposals.location: mixmogam/twostep.py:fit_variance_components/_KOp (new dense operator); mixmogam/_loco.py:raw_slices
proposals.mechanism: G = z' W z (unprojected, n x n float32) is built once. Decoded slices are scaled by sqrt(w) and accumulated with scipy ssyrk (beta=1, upper triangle, F-order, so no n x n temporary), then mirrored in blocks. Each Lanczos step is then project(G @ project(P)) / sum(w), a 2.45-GFLOP dense GEMM at n=5000, instead of a full decode plus two narrow GEMMs over m variants. The build costs about one ssyrk-efficient pass, about 2.4x cheaper than 24 streaming passes per variant at n=5000.
proposals.evidence: Prototype: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/pre-vb/dense_reml.py, bench_reml.py, crossover.py and e2e.py. Wide REML only: streaming 2.86-4.47 s against dense 1.55-1.85 s, median ratio 0.543. Per variant, the build costs 30.6 us (4096-row chunks) or 34.8 us (default 838-row slices); 24 streaming passes cost 81 us. A fixed 0.45 s goes to 24 dense products plus the grid. Complete gwas() on wide REML, 5 pairs: ratio 0.833, saves 1.48 s. h2 changes by 1.3e-8, max |dlog10 p| 8.6e-7, lambda_GC unchanged to 6 decimals, no decision changes. With adaptive stopping and stacked HE also applied: ratio 0.755 and max |dlog10 p| 9.1e-7. Crossover with m=6000: build plus 24 products divided by 24 streaming passes is 0.68 at n=5000, 0.87 at 6500, 1.17 at 8000 (worse at small m). Scaled to P3: 0.39 x 26.9 + 0.45, about 10.8 s against 26.9 s. Peak footprint on wide went from 217 to 277 MB.
proposals.memory_effect: Adds n^2*4 bytes, freed before the VB fits (100 MB at n=5000). At P3 full size the process peak should not grow, because VB then holds a Gram cache of about 0.93 GiB. On the reduced wide panel the peak grew by 60 MB (217 to 277 MB). Gate it on n^2*4 <= min(gram_cache_bytes, the VB cache this run will actually fill).
proposals.risks: Largely redundant with adaptive stopping. At P3, 8-9 streaming passes (about 9-10 s) already cost less than the dense build (about 10 s), so its extra saving with adaptive stopping adopted is about 0. It remains useful where Lanczos needs many steps at small n, and under strong structure, where the 6-pass x 140-column deflation basis would also become cheap. A first prototype mirror skipped the lower triangles of the diagonal blocks and gave a non-symmetric G; the current blocked mirror is checked (G == G.T, relative error 4.6e-7 against float64). Needs an n/m cost model, not a fixed n threshold.

proposals.title: Lanczos bookkeeping: store the Krylov basis per run, (r, steps, n), so full reorthogonalization uses batched BLAS GEMVs instead of einsum
proposals.location: mixmogam/_slq.py:lanczos_quadrature_batch
proposals.mechanism: Full reorthogonalization currently does two einsum contractions over Q[:j+1] (steps, n, r) at about 21 GB/s, plus several n x r temporaries per step: W allocation, fancy-index copy, np.where normalization. Storing each run's basis contiguously lets coef = B @ w and w -= B' coef run as batched matmul (BLAS gemv), with in-place normalization. Same arithmetic up to summation order.
proposals.evidence: Prototype: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/pre-vb/lanczos_fast.py and bench_lanczos.py. With a cheap operator so the bookkeeping is isolated, 24 steps, r=49: n=20,000 went from 0.716 to 0.423 s (ratio 0.59) and n=50,000 from 1.899 to 1.206 s (ratio 0.63). Rule values agree to 2e-14 relative. In-process REML on tall, 6 pairs: ratio 0.88 (noisy, machine load about 6). Tall REML h2 changed by 1.3e-15, and complete gwas() on tall (with stacked HE) had max |dlog10 p| 2e-13. The HAPNEST profile has 1.1-1.9 s of Lanczos overhead (lanczos tottime 0.6 + einsum 0.58 + projections). Scaled: about 0.7 s at HAPNEST with 24 steps, about 0.3 s if adaptive stopping is adopted (the reorthogonalization cost grows with j^2), about 0.1 s at P3.
proposals.memory_effect: Same basis size (float64, r x steps x n); fewer transient n x r arrays per step.
proposals.risks: The column layout transposes the operator's input and output each step (one n x r copy). Breakdown handling must keep the inactive-column semantics; the prototype keeps them but only exercised the no-breakdown path.

proposals.title: Drop the redundant covariate projections around the streaming kinship in the REML operator
proposals.location: mixmogam/lmm.py:LMM._reml_op; mixmogam/twostep.py:_KOp; mixmogam/_loco.py:_products
proposals.mechanism: lmm._reml_op projects x before kdot and projects Kx afterwards. LocoGenotypes._products already projects P (Pt = project(P)) and the result (project(total)) with a bitwise-identical Q, the QR of the same st.X. So two of the four n x r projections per pass are idempotent re-projections. A flag on the operator (e.g. _KOp.projects_covariates = True) would let _reml_op skip them.
proposals.evidence: Not measured on its own. The HAPNEST REML profile shows lmm.mv tottime 0.29 s over 24 passes, which is the two inline projections at n=50k x 49, plus _loco.project 0.30 s. Removing the outer pair saves about mv's tottime: about 0.29 s at 24 passes (about 0.17 s with adaptive stopping) and about 0.02 s at P3 (mv tottime 0.024 s).
proposals.memory_effect: Slightly less: two fewer n x r float64 temporaries per pass.
proposals.risks: This couples LMM to an operator promise. A wrong flag (an operator that does not project, or a different covariate basis, e.g. weighted vs unweighted Q) would silently fit the wrong operator, so the flag must be set only by _KOp built from the same st.

proposals.title: Tiled variant-major prepare_moments kernel (from the roadmap)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_standardize.py:_moments_tile/_moments_columns_serial
proposals.mechanism: The current int8 kernel loops samples-outer, variants-inner with strided scalar gathers (about 1.7 ns per call at P3). The roadmap's variant-major kernel counts per column and transposes 64 x 256 tiles, keeping each variant's summation order, so values are identical.
proposals.evidence: Not re-measured here. The roadmap reports 1.35-1.4x with identical values (slower for two-bit calls). Scaled by the profiles' prepare_moments tottime: P3 3.43 s x (1 - 1/1.375) = 0.94 s in both P3 profiles; HAPNEST 1.77 s x 0.27 = 0.48 s.
proposals.memory_effect: Adds a 64 x 256 tile buffer per worker (negligible).
proposals.risks: Must keep the sequential per-variant order for thread-count invariance. The two-bit packed path does not gain, so keep the current packed kernel.

propose:variance.notes:
Interactions:
(1) Adaptive stopping and the dense kinship target the same P3 REML cost and mostly do not add up. With adaptive stopping, P3 needs 8-9 streaming passes (about 9-10 s), which is already below the dense build (about 10 s at n=5000). Count about 17 s for the pair, not 33 s. The dense path is only worth keeping for small-n cases that still need many steps, or for strong structure (cheap deflation basis).
(2) The Lanczos-bookkeeping and redundant-projection savings shrink with adaptive stopping (about 0.3 s and 0.17 s at HAPNEST instead of 0.7 s and 0.29 s).
(3) The HE stacked GEMM is independent and bit-identical.
Expected default-path total: about 18 s of 56.6 s at P3-REML and about 7.8 s of 43.8 s at HAPNEST-REML. HE paths gain only the HE-pass and prepare_moments items (about 0.5-1.4 s).

Measured and rejected (no proposal):
(a) Accumulating the backward GEMM in float32 inside BLAS (scipy sgemm beta=1, float64 flush every 16 slices) to drop the per-slice float64 add: REML-only ABAB on tall gave ratio 1.005. No gain. Prototype in acc_products.py.
(b) Fewer SLQ probes or columns: per-slice GEMM cost is nearly flat in column count (17 columns = 0.82-0.90 of 49; cols_rate2.py), so fewer probes barely saves time. Passes are the lever, not columns.
(c) Computing REML's first Lanczos product inside the HE pass: with 5 alphas the backward width grows from 170 to about 415 columns, costing roughly the one REML pass it saves. Net about 0, and it couples the APIs.
(d) A float32 cache of decoded rows across REML passes: about 0.9 s at HAPNEST for about 1 GB of memory there. Not justified.

Accuracy notes:
- Monte Carlo SD of SLQ h2 across probe seeds (48 probes) was 2-6e-3. Lanczos truncation at 24 steps was 3e-15 (n/m 0.125) and 7e-7 (n/m 2.5) against 64 steps, so the existing 24-step default is accurate.
- An earlier run of my steps study showed an apparent 8e-4 truncation bias. It came from a bug in my prototype's blocked mirror and is withdrawn.
- One HAPNEST-subset run briefly reached about 1.95 GB peak footprint (a float64 copy for phenotype simulation) before I switched to a lean script (252 MB). No other process exceeded about 1.1 GB.
- All timings were taken under load average 5-7 with other agents running, ABAB in-process.

Scripts are in /tmp/hratt-speed/work/pre-vb/: e2e.py (complete-gwas ABAB plus equivalence), variants.py (installers), bench_reml_patch.py, hapnest_subset.py (mmap BED subset, n=12,500 x 5,000).

Production note for adaptive stopping: run the convergence check through _slq_pack's closures so deflation, ML and alpha_method='reml' are covered, vectorize it over rules, and expose a tolerance where 0 means the old fixed 24 steps.

proposals.title: Separate, looser stopping tolerance for the CV grid fit (cv_tol = 10 x vb_tol = 1e-4)
proposals.location: mixmogam/twostep.py:_hratt_fit_scores (CV eng.fit call), hratt signature (new cv_tol kwarg)
proposals.mechanism: The 10-column CV fit only decides argmin of hold-out MSE, but it is run to the same 1e-5 criterion as the LOCO fits. Slow sparse columns (p = 0.01) drag it on for many extra sweeps after the ranking has settled. Each sweep is dominated by fixed per-sweep costs: decoding, GEMM reads of Z, Gram reads and per-block overhead. Stopping the CV at max rel < 1e-4 removes whole sweeps. The LOCO fit is untouched, so p-values are bit-identical whenever the same grid model is chosen.
proposals.evidence:
Prototype in /tmp/hratt-speed/work/budget (xfit.py, xscores.py, time_abab.py; run_cvtraj.py with analyze_cv.py, analyze_tau.py and analyze_conv.py).

CV sweeps: wide panel 13 -> 8 (HE and REML); tall panel 7 -> 5 (HE and REML). LOCO sweeps unchanged. p-values bit-identical on wide/tall x HE/REML and on wide with 4 covariates.

Selection check: 54 CV trajectories run to tol 1e-7 (2 panels x 5 architectures [bench, polygenic, sparse, mixed low-h2, very sparse] x phenotype seeds x 3 random_states). Tol 1e-4 kept the same model in 54/54 and cut CV sweeps 22% (wide-bench runs 37 -> 23). Tol 3e-4 also kept 54/54 (-33%); tol 1e-3 flipped one (53/54). The smallest tolerance at which any run would have flipped was 3.5e-4. Both 1e-5 and 1e-4 matched the converged (1e-7) choice in 54/54.

Paired timings (stock fit, CPU time, machine load 6-7): wide HE ratio 0.878 (-0.78 s of 5.94; expected 5 sweeps x 0.155 s); tall HE ratio 0.922 (-0.32 s).

Scaling: per-sweep CV cost from the profiles (fit cumtime minus Gram prep and predict, split CV:LOCO by the reduced-panel ratios) is 1.55 s at p3 and 0.70-0.80 s at hapnest. Expected sweeps saved: p3-he 5 -> 4; p3-reml 4 -> 3 or 4 (expected value about 0.5 sweep); hapnest 12 -> about 8 (it has the slow-tail pattern of the wide-bench runs, 12-13 -> 7-8).
proposals.memory_effect: None (fewer sweeps over the same arrays).
proposals.risks:
This is an algorithmic default change. It is bit-identical only while the chosen grid model is unchanged; that held in 54/54 trajectories plus 7 complete runs. A flip would pick a near-tied model (MSE within about 0.1%, far below the hold-out's sampling error of 3-6%), but it moves top-hit p-values by up to about 0.9 log10 (seen with an unsafe per-column variant).

extra['cv_mse'] changes slightly and cv_converged then refers to cv_tol. Should be documented in the CHANGELOG. Not tested on binary or weighted traits. The full-size sweep counts are extrapolated, not measured.
proposals.saving_multicore_note: Sweep count drops for every thread count; HRATT gains only 1.04x from 4 cores, so the seconds saved stay about the same.

proposals.title: Build the CV and cross-fit Gram caches in one pass when all 7 slots fit the Gram budget
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py:VBEngine._prepare_grams/_gram; twostep.py:_hratt_fit_scores (one engine for both fits)
proposals.mechanism:
Today two engines each decode every sub-block and form float64 Grams: the CV engine (full product plus a masked gather for the 10% hold-out, 1.1 n k^2) and the cross-fit engine (fold partition, 1.0 n k^2).

One pass over the cross-fit partition can produce slots [full, train_0..4] exactly as now, plus train_cv = full - Z_held Z_held' (corrected the same way), with the held columns gathered from the already-widened fold-sorted block. The CV fit then reads slot train_cv and the LOCO fit reads slots 0..5. This removes the CV engine's Gram flops, its gather and one decode pass. The stock fit only needs gidx to address an arbitrary slot (the prototype used contiguous views).
proposals.evidence:
Prototype: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/budget/shared.py, time_shared.py.

Tall HE (6 pairs): whole run -0.60 s (ratio 0.89, load 6); Gram prep 0.63 (CV) + 0.89 (LOCO) -> 0.96 s.
Wide HE (4 pairs): -0.26 s (ratio 0.95); prep 0.35 + 0.48 -> 0.56 s; fit time unchanged (3.20 vs 3.18 s).

p-values bit-identical (wide HE/REML, tall HE). The LOCO Grams replicate the partition path operation by operation; cv_mse relative difference is at most 9e-16.

A first version with a strided CV view of the Gram array was 1.7 s slower on wide (Numba 'A'-layout sweep), so contiguous slot access matters.

Scaling: hapnest Gram prep is 4.62 s for both engines; the CV share is about 45% (2.1 s) minus about 0.25 s for the held Gram, giving about 1.8 s. At p3, 7 slots need about 1.46 GB, over the 1e9 budget (the LOCO engine already caches only 2,518 of 3,140 sub-blocks), so it must fall back to separate engines: no saving there.
proposals.memory_effect: Peak Gram storage goes from 6 slots (LOCO engine) to 7 (+17%; about 62 -> 72 MB at hapnest). It is used only when all 7 slots fit gram_cache_bytes, so peak stays within the budget. The CV engine's separate 2-slot cache and decode buffer disappear.
proposals.risks:
CV Grams differ at float64 rounding, because the full Gram is a sum over folds rather than a direct product. A selection flip would need an exact near-tie.

Applies only to the cross-fit path (loco_folds >= 2, refit False or True) and only when the cache fits, so p3-sized panels keep two engines. A compact (symmetric-half) Gram storage proposal would make it apply at p3 as well. Needs care with the parallel GEMM workspace and the _warn_on_partial semantics.
proposals.saving_multicore_note: Gram preparation is serial today, so the saving is unchanged with 4-10 cores (larger share of the shorter run).

proposals.title: Score the CV hold-out from the fit's own residual updates instead of a final predict pass
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py:VBEngine.fit (optional held-index tracking); twostep.py:_hratt_fit_scores (mse from tracked image, _compute_prediction=False for the CV)
proposals.mechanism:
The CV fit ends with VBEngine.predict: a full float64 decode pass plus GEMMs, and it also builds (n, 10) prediction and resid arrays, only to compute hold-out MSE on 10% of samples. The backward GEMM already produces z'd for every sample, held-out ones included (the residual refresh just masks them).

A small Numba loop over the held indices per block (Hres[h, p] -= delta[held[h], p]) keeps y - z'beta on the hold-out. MSE is then that image plus Q_held A. The fit's own arithmetic is untouched.
proposals.evidence:
Prototype: xfit.py (_held_track, track_mode=2).

Tracked vs predict-based hold-out MSE: relative difference 1.3-2.3e-8 on all four panel/method runs. The smallest model gap in the 54 trajectories was 4.3e-5 relative, so the margin is over 2,000x. p-values bit-identical.

Paired whole-run savings are within noise but consistent in sign: wide -0.19 s, tall -0.10 s (wide predict is 0.09 s by timer).

Scaling: predict costs 0.84 s at p3 and 0.45 s at hapnest (profiles). Tracking costs n_held x 10 x blocks x sweeps updates: about 0.06 s at p3, about 0.1 s at hapnest.
proposals.memory_effect: Slightly lower. It avoids two (n, 10) float64 arrays (prediction and resid: 0.8 MB at p3, 8 MB at hapnest) and the 16 MiB predict tile buffer, and adds an n_held x 10 float64 image (0.04 / 0.4 MB).
proposals.risks: cv_mse changes at about 1e-8 relative (float32-rounded updates, which the fit's own residual already uses). The in-sample loco_folds=1 path, and the stage1='auto' comparison of held-out MSE against LDpred3, should use the same estimator consistently.

proposals.title: Compile the rank-q covariate corrections of each sub-block (one Numba call for all column sets)
proposals.area: VB per-block overhead (found while instrumenting the sweep budget)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py:VBEngine.fit (the 'for g_val, cols in column_sets' blocks before the sweep and after the backward GEMM)
proposals.mechanism: The LOCO fit has 5 column sets (one per fold), and each sub-block runs about 60 small NumPy calls for the covariate corrections, about 100 us per block. Two small Numba kernels (pre: Ub += T A - c(s + train A); post: e, W, s_proj, change, A) replace them. The work is k x q x P flops.
proposals.evidence:
Prototype: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/budget/qcorr.py and xfit.py qnumba option; run_qn.py and run_qn_cov.py.

Wide HE, 3 interleaved reps under load:
- LOCO correction time 0.250 -> 0.026 s over 7 sweeps (about 100 -> 10 us per block-visit).
- CV 0.131 -> 0.065 s over 13 sweeps.
- LOCO fit 1.26 -> 0.95 s.

p-values bit-identical with q = 1. With 4 extra covariates (q = 5), max |dlog10 p| = 1.4e-14.

Scaling (idle about 0.8x the loaded numbers): about 80 us per LOCO block-visit x 3,140 blocks x 4 sweeps = 1.0 s, plus CV about 13 us x 3,140 x 5 = 0.2 s at p3. Hapnest has 157 blocks: about 0.13 s.
proposals.memory_effect: None (a q x q per-slot train array instead of a dict).
proposals.risks: Fixed-order loops replace BLAS sums over k, so rounding changes with q > 1. Likely overlaps with any proposer working on VB per-block overhead. Strong-structure refit (100 LOCO columns) still has 5 column sets, so the saving per block is similar.
proposals.saving_multicore_note: Python overhead is serial; the saving is unchanged with more cores.

proposals.title: Optional: freeze converged CV columns at 1e-5 and drop clearly dominated grid columns (>1% worse hold-out MSE from sweep 3)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py:VBEngine.fit (active-column set), twostep.py:_hratt_fit_scores
proposals.mechanism: Columns stop sweeping once their own rel < 1e-5, the exact precision the current rule demands of the slowest column. Columns whose tracked hold-out MSE exceeds the current best by more than 1% after sweep 3 are frozen at their current value. Active columns are compacted, so the Numba sweep, refresh and GEMM widths shrink. This needs the held tracking of the hold-out-scoring proposal. It sits on top of the CV-tolerance proposal and mainly removes column-sweeps, not whole sweeps.
proposals.evidence:
Offline on the 54 trajectories:
- Freeze at 1e-5 alone: 54/54 same model, 18% fewer column-sweeps.
- Prune 1% + freeze 1e-5 + stop 1e-4: 54/54, 25% fewer sweeps and 39% fewer column-sweeps, against 22%/22% for the 1e-4 stop alone.
- Freezing at 1e-4 per column is unsafe: on wide HE it switched (0.1,0.3) -> (0.1,0.1), max |dlog10 p| 0.93.

Paired timings:
- Wide: freeze only -0.16 s (ratio 0.974).
- Wide: freeze 1e-5 + stop 1e-4 + tracking -1.02 s (0.803), against -0.78 s for the 1e-4 stop alone.
- Tall: prune + freeze + stop + tracking -0.59 s (0.840), against -0.57 s without pruning.
- p-values bit-identical in all 6 complete runs.

Scaling: about 20% of the remaining CV column-sweeps x about 70 ms (p3, Numba-heavy) or about 25 ms (hapnest, GEMM/refresh) per column-sweep gives about 0.4 s each.
proposals.memory_effect: None (compaction can permute active columns to the front in place; the prototype copied the small n x P arrays).
proposals.risks: The 1% margin is a heuristic with thin evidence (a 0.3% margin from sweep 2 failed 2/54). A sparse model that improves late could be dropped. The gain is small next to the CV-tolerance proposal and shrinks with column-parallel Numba threads. Low priority.
proposals.saving_multicore_note: Column-parallel sweeps already spread per-column work, so with 4-10 cores the gain mostly vanishes.

proposals.title: Not recommended: warm-start the cross-fitted LOCO fits from the CV fit's chosen-model effects
proposals.location: twostep.py:_hratt_fit_scores; _vb.py:VBEngine.fit (beta0 plus residual image)
proposals.mechanism: Start each fold's fit from beta_cv[:, best], with the residual initialised for free from the CV fit's own residual image (no predict pass). This cuts LOCO sweeps but leaks information: beta_cv was fit on 90% of samples, including most of fold f, whose out-of-fold scores the fold-f fit must not see. At finite tolerance the endpoint remembers the start.
proposals.evidence:
Wide HE:
- LOCO sweeps 7 -> 4.
- vs baseline: max |dlog10 p| 0.050, lambda_GC 1.0818 -> 1.0813, significant at 0.05/m 29 -> 28 (one flip).
- At tol 1e-7, warm vs cold differ by only 0.0064, so the gap is a finite-tolerance memory of the start, not a different fixed point.

proposals.memory_effect: Adds an (m, k) start array (same size as beta).
proposals.risks: Breaks the out-of-fold property of cross-fitting at finite tolerance: in-sample absorption, as with loco_folds=1. The error is 3.5x the existing tolerance noise. Do not adopt.

proposals.title: Not recommended: loosen the LOCO tolerance (1e-5 -> 3e-5 or 1e-4)
proposals.location: twostep.py:_hratt_fit_scores (LOCO eng.fit tol)
proposals.mechanism: Stop the cross-fit one sweep earlier. LOCO convergence is near-superlinear (rel 1.5e-3, 6e-5, 2e-6), so both looser tolerances save exactly one sweep.
proposals.evidence:
Wide HE: 7 -> 6 LOCO sweeps; max |dlog10 p| 0.0077; lambda_GC 1.08182 -> 1.08186; no 0.05/m flips.

The default itself is 0.014 from a 1e-7-converged fit (one 0.05/m flip), so loosening adds about 50% more convergence error. Scaled: one LOCO sweep, 2.2 s at p3 (including the Gram recompute) and 0.56 s at hapnest.
proposals.memory_effect: None
proposals.risks: Reduces the accuracy of the LOCO scores, which already carry about 0.01 log10 p of tolerance noise. If anything, a tighter LOCO tolerance is the statistically safer direction. Needs a user decision.

propose:iterations.notes:
Measurement conditions: the machine ran at load average 5-7 throughout (other agents), so complete runs were about 1.25x slower than the idle baselines. I relied on interleaved medians (wall and CPU time agreed) plus component accounting.

Full-size per-sweep costs come from the profiles, using _subblocks call counts to separate the fits:
- p3-he: 9 sweeps, CV 5 + LOCO 4.
- p3-reml: CV 4 + LOCO 4.
- hapnest: CV 12 + LOCO 8.
- CV sweep about 1.55 s at p3 and 0.70-0.80 s at hapnest; LOCO sweep about 2.2 s at p3 (including 0.74 s of uncached Gram recompute) and 0.56 s at hapnest.

Full-size CV sweep reductions are extrapolated from the reduced panels, not measured.

Interactions:
(1) The CV-tolerance proposal and the optional freeze/prune proposal overlap. The freeze/prune saving is quoted on top of the tolerance change, and per-column freezing must stay at 1e-5: freezing at 1e-4 flipped the model.
(2) Freeze/prune needs the held-out tracking from the hold-out-scoring proposal.
(3) Shared Gram preparation is skipped at p3 because 7 slots exceed the 1e9 budget. It would apply there if another proposer halves Gram storage (symmetric storage) or the budget changes. It shrinks if Gram preparation itself gets faster (e.g. a compiled fold gather). Its prototype also showed that strided Gram views cost about 1.7 s on wide, so slots must be addressed contiguously (generalise gidx).
(4) The compiled covariate corrections are outside the budget area and may duplicate a per-block-overhead proposal.
(5) bolt's 90-column CV (BOLT_GRID x folds) could use the same separate CV tolerance.

Considered and rejected:
- Over-relaxed sweeps (omega 1.1-1.5): CV 13 -> 12/11/10/17 sweeps but LOCO 7 -> 7/8/9/14; max |dlog10 p| 0.006-0.02. Not worth it.
- Merging the CV tail with speculative LOCO columns: needs 7 slots, and once the CV tolerance is relaxed it no longer pays.
- Using cross-fit fold 0 as the CV hold-out (20% hold-out): an estimator change, dominated by the bit-identical shared Gram preparation, and neutral at p3 because of cache recomputes.

Statistical observation: on the wide panel the default LOCO tolerance (1e-5) is already 0.014 log10 p from the converged fit, with one 0.05/m flip.

proposals.title: Keep Numba's OpenMP workers warm during VB fits (libomp blocktime ~1 ms)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: _numba_thread_limit / VBEngine.fit (around the sweep loop when n_threads > 1)
proposals.mechanism: In this env Numba uses the omp layer with LLVM libomp, and kmp_get_blocktime() returns 0, so workers sleep after every parallel region. Each launch then costs about 34-40 us (4 threads, empty kernel) instead of about 4 us. A VB fit at n_threads>1 makes two launches per 128-SNP sub-block (parallel decode and the column-parallel sweep), each with only 100-200 us of work. Wake-ups therefore eat most of the gain, which is why HRATT at n=5,000 sees ~1.0x from 4 workers. The fix calls kmp_set_blocktime(1) through ctypes, but only when threading_layer()=='omp' and the symbol exists, and restores the old value when the fit exits. Do not set it process-wide: spinning workers then slowed the BLAS-threaded SLQ passes (wide REML _products went from 1.69 to 2.07 s with VECLIB=4).
proposals.evidence: Launch overhead, empty prange kernel, 4 threads: 39.8 us at the default (blocktime 0), 3.9 us at 1 ms, 4.0 us at 200 ms (launch2.py). Complete HRATT, 9 interleaved pairs, bit-identical p: wide HE (5k x 40k, cache 1e8, VECLIB=1) b1 5.28 / b4 5.10 / b4+blocktime 4.24 s, so blocktime gives 1.20x over current nt=4. Tall HE 2.69 -> 2.48 s. Wide REML 7.50 -> 6.71 s. Tall REML 6.15 -> 5.85 s. Blocktime of 1, 5 or 20 ms made no difference. VB sweep phase on wide: 3.39 -> 2.89 s over 6,400 sub-block iterations, about 78 us each; tall about 143 us each over 1,040 iterations. Scaling: p3 has about 28,400 VB sub-block iterations (from 37,441 decode calls minus prep and streaming), so 2.3 s. HAPNEST about 3,140 iterations, so 0.5 s. Logs: /tmp/hratt-speed/work/multicore/suite_*_vl1.log, bt_wide.log, bt_tall.log, bdreml4_wide.log.
proposals.saving_multicore_note: Every saving here is against the current code at n_threads=4. The single-thread saving is zero (the change only runs when n_threads>1). Alone, it took wide HE from 1.03x to 1.25x over one thread.
proposals.memory_effect: none; workers spin up to 1 ms after a launch (CPU only)
proposals.risks: Private libomp API through ctypes: it must no-op on the workqueue/tbb layers, libgomp or a missing symbol. The setting is per calling thread, so Python helper threads keep their own. Spinning workers compete with helper and BLAS threads, so keep it scoped to VB fits.

proposals.title: Prefetch the next VB sub-block (decode + uncached Gram) in a helper thread; nogil sweep/refresh/decode kernels
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: VBEngine.fit sub-block loop (+ nogil=True on _sweep_block, _sweep_block_parallel, _refresh_residual); mixmogam/_standardize.py decode kernels nogil=True
proposals.mechanism: While the main thread runs sub-block b (forward GEMM, sweep, backward GEMM, residual refresh), one helper thread does two things for sub-block b+1. It decodes it into a second buffer with the serial nogil kernel. If that sub-block falls outside the Gram cache (20% of LOCO sub-blocks at p3), it also builds its Gram. Making the Numba kernels nogil lets the two threads overlap, and the arithmetic is unchanged. The helper never launches parallel Numba regions, so the workqueue layer is safe. At n=5,000, parallel decode of 128 rows was only 110 -> 101 us anyway, because it is memory bound.
proposals.evidence: Prototype in /tmp/hratt-speed/work/multicore/vb_proto.py (VBX._stream) and allpatch.py. Grams, betas and p are bit-identical in every run. On wide HE (cache 1e8, which mimics p3's 80% cached LOCO) at nt=4 with blocktime, the VB sweep phase went 2.89 -> 2.70 s (bd2_wide_he.log), about 30 us per sub-block iteration. On tall (n=20k) there was no measurable gain (sweep phase 0.94 vs 0.97 s); two 10 MB buffers exceed L2 there. Scaling: p3 is about 28,400 iterations x 30 us = 0.85 s. HAPNEST is about 0. Running nogil kernels at n_threads=1 cost nothing (paired 0.999x and 0.989x, bit-identical; nt1_check.py).
proposals.saving_multicore_note: Measured against current nt=4. Engage it only when n_threads>1, because it needs a second core. Most of the combined gain already appears at n_threads=2 (see notes).
proposals.memory_effect: +1 sub-block buffer (128 x n x 4 B: 2.5 MB at n=5k, 25.6 MB at n=50k). Uncached-Gram transients move to the helper, so their peak is unchanged.
proposals.risks: Oversubscription at high thread counts. An earlier variant with 8 Numba threads, global blocktime and the helper ran 1.02x on wide against 1.19x without the helper. When the helper runs, cap the Numba width at n_threads-1. Generator close and exceptions must join the pending future before the buffers are reused.

proposals.title: Parallel Gram preparation across sub-blocks (memory-budgeted workers)
proposals.location: mixmogam/_vb.py: VBEngine._prepare_grams (+ build _fold_layout before the pool)
proposals.mechanism: The cached sub-blocks are known before any work starts, because their sizes are deterministic. Each worker decodes its own sub-block (serial nogil kernel, own buffer) and calls _gram, and the results are stored in order. Gram GEMMs, casts and gathers release the GIL. propose:parallel.notes:
The main finding: HRATT at n=5,000 does not scale with n_threads mainly because of libomp wake-ups. kmp_get_blocktime() is 0 in this env, so each Numba parallel launch costs about 35-40 us, and a VB fit makes two such launches per 128-SNP sub-block. Fixing that, plus the overlaps above, made n_threads=4 1.37-1.56x faster than one thread on the reduced panels. The current code manages 1.11-1.18x. All p-values were bit-identical.

**Combined prototype ("final")**
- Blocktime is set only inside VB fits.
- Streaming slices and VB sub-blocks are prefetched; Grams are prepared in parallel; the _he_alpha alpha loop runs on a pool.
- It does not include the REML CV-prep overlap or the BLAS guidance change.
- Measured with 7 interleaved pairs at load about 2-2.5 (final_*.log):

| Panel and method | b1 (1 thread) | b4 (current nt=4) | final2 (2 threads) | final4 (4 threads) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wide HE, VECLIB=1 | 5.15 | 4.64 | 3.96 | 3.81 (1.37x) |
| tall HE, VECLIB=1 | 3.20 | 2.71 | 2.36 | 2.05 (1.56x) |
| wide REML, VECLIB=4 | 7.80 | 6.60 | 5.86 | 5.63 (1.37x) |
| tall REML, VECLIB=4 | 6.47 | 5.62 | 5.27 | 4.96 (1.31x) |

Times are seconds; the bracketed factor is against b1. Most of the gain already appears with two threads.

**Equivalence and single-thread checks**
- All runs compared p-values, Grams and betas exactly.
- Every proposal is gated on n_threads>1, so the one-thread path is unchanged.
- Recompiling the kernels with nogil=True cost nothing at nt=1 (0.99-1.00x, bit-identical).

**Scaled estimates for the full profiles** (component shares, against current code at n_threads=4)
- p3-HE: about 5.5 s (blocktime 2.3, prefetch 0.85, parallel Gram 1.6, _he_alpha pool 0.7). That is about 18%, consistent with wide's measured 18%.
- p3-REML: about 5.5 s, plus about 1.9 s from overlapping the CV Grams with REML, plus about 3 s from BLAS threads.
- HAPNEST-HE: about 3.4 s (about 20%; tall measured 24%).
- HAPNEST-REML: about 4.5 s, plus about 1.1 s overlap, plus about 4 s BLAS.
- The proposals overlap, so their savings are not fully additive. Prefetch and parallel prep both shorten the CV prep that the REML overlap would hide.

**Measured no-gos (not proposed)**
- Lowering _GEMM_MIN_SAMPLES to 0 at n=20k: 1.00-1.05x, and betas change at about 1e-7.
- Setting blocktime process-wide: it slowed the BLAS-threaded SLQ passes (wide _products 1.69 to 2.07 s).
- Global helpers at 8 threads: oversubscription (wide 1.02x against 1.19x for blocktime alone). Cap the Numba width at n_threads-1 when a helper runs.
- Parallel SLQ passes: not possible, because Lanczos steps are sequential and the probes are already batched.
- Parallel decode of 128-row VB sub-blocks at n=5k: only 110 to 101 us, because it is memory bound.

**Interaction with the roadmap's compiled gather-and-widen item.** NumPy's `Zs[:, order].astype(float64)` returns an F-ordered array. The fold GEMMs' rounding depends on that layout: a C-order compiled replacement changed the float64 coefficients, although the float32 Grams stayed equal. A compiled kernel that writes F-order output is bit-identical (verified in gram_bench.py) and drops the float32 gathered copy (4·k·n bytes per Gram).

**Measurement caveats**
- Load was 5-8 from other agents for the first two hours, and those 4-thread runs were badly biased. Under that load, current nt=4 was slower than nt=1.
- The final suite ran at load 2-2.5.
- The REML BLAS comparison crosses processes, because Accelerate's runtime switch was unreliable.
- I accidentally ran a fuzzy `pkill -f "until grep -q"`. It may have stopped another agent's wait loop.

**Files** (all under /tmp/hratt-speed/work/multicore/)
- Prototypes: allpatch.py (combined patches, VBFinal, he_alpha_final), vb_proto.py (VBX), nogil.py, he_alpha_par.py.
- Drivers: full_ab.py, breakdown2.py, gram_bench.py, products_bench.py, overlap_reml.py, launch2.py, kern_bench.py, gemm_min.py.
- Logs: final_*.log, suite_*.log, bd2_wide_he.log, bt_*.log, bdreml4_*.log, nt8_*.log.

Equivalence: rounding-level; max |dlog10 p| 1.5e-6 (wide), 5.1e-6 (tall); lambda_GC within 1e-6; 0 of 29/186 decisions at 0.05/m changed; same CV choice. Scaling: p3 SLQ 26.9 s / 24 = 1.12 s per pass x 15-16 passes saved minus ~0.1 s checks = ~17 s; hapnest 19.1/24 = 0.8 s x 9-10 passes minus 0.35 s = ~7 s. HE path unaffected. verify:C7.problems:
1) As written, the proposer's prototype sends every np.ndarray through the column kernels. On sample-major (C-order) int8 that is 4.5x slower (14.4 against 3.2 ns/call). It must be limited to variant-major input, and sample-major and strided layouts must either build the same centered tile (via a transpose) or keep the old kernel.

2) Keeping the old kernel for some layouts or for packed calls breaks the existing identical-values tests: test_preparation_and_decoding_ignore_storage_order (C/F/strided/packed) and the packed-vs-int8 test in test_loco_prepared_moments. Every format has to fill the same 64 x n tile and make the same BLAS call. A2 shows packed and int8 then agree exactly.

3) The proposer's prototype falls back for sq_weights, so binary traits (always weighted) and sampling weights got no saving. A fused centered decode that also sums sqw*c^2 (fastmath) recovers 2.05-2.24x at rounding level (zz relative difference up to 1.8e-14). A separate weighted-count kernel was 0.57x, slower than the original, so this needs care. No second BLAS product is needed.

4) Packed calls reach only 1.3x with the original histogram count loop. A popcount-style two-bit counter is needed to get about 2x.

5) Accelerate's per-row result depends on how many variants share a tile: a one-row product differs from the same row inside a 64-row product (verified). Coefficients therefore depend on the tile composition at block ends and on the BLAS library and version. The module and prepare_moments docstrings promise "each variant sums its samples in order whatever the tile"; that promise has to change. Fixed 64-variant tiles keep thread-count invariance (verified identical at 1 and 4 threads).

6) The tile is 8n bytes x 64 per thread: 2.6 MB at 5k and 25.6 MB at 50k, transient and before any Gram cache, so peak RSS is unchanged. At n=500k it would be 256 MB per thread, beyond the 64 MB _STANDARDIZE_WORK_BYTES budget. The tile width must be capped as a function of n alone, not the thread count, to stay thread-invariant.

7) The prototype is serial, so n_threads is ignored. On a loaded machine, serial A was still 1.14-1.2x faster than the original's 4-thread kernel. My Python thread pool barely scaled, so a parallel version should do the scalar work in Numba prange; Numba's np.dot gave results identical to NumPy @ here.

8) The strong-structure path amplifies the change to 1.4e-6 in log10 p. That is intrinsic (a random 2e-13 perturbation does the same) and changes no decision, but it is not 1e-13.

9) With q=0 (GenotypeKinship) the centered decode should be skipped.

10) Python per-tile overhead (6,250 tiles at p3) is inside the measured numbers; moving it into Numba would gain slightly more.

11) The saving is a one-off per fit: about 5% of p3-HE and 2-4% elsewhere, small against the KVIK gap.

1) The budget split is load-bearing. The proposer's joint.py caches both engines per sub-block or neither. When the budget binds, that is slower than stock. Wide HE at gram_cache_bytes=2e7: wall 0.97x, Gram work 12.7 -> 13.9 s, because the CV fit now rebuilds sub-blocks the stock CV engine kept. With CV-first allocation the same run gives wall 1.41x and Gram 14.6 -> 8.4 s, with identical p-values. The budget also binds earlier than "above about 620k variants" suggests. Both packed caches cost about 3,140 x (198 KB + 8.2 KB x q), which passes 1e9 at p3 scale once q reaches about 15 covariate columns, for example 10 PCs plus a few covariates. CV-first must be in the implementation, not a footnote. The slot-0 coefficients (S = zQ) are stored twice, once per cache; with many covariates the float64 coefficients are a large share of the cache and could be shared.

2) The proposer's prototype replaces only the serial _sweep_block. With n_threads > 1, fit calls _sweep_block_parallel with packed 2-D Grams, so a packed prange kernel is required. Mine has one: p-values were identical with 2 threads, including the strong-structure refit, and it was not slower (1.46x wall under load).

3) The CV-phase memory peak rises because the LOCO cache is held during the CV fit: at p3 about 0.42 -> 0.64 GB. The global peak falls (about 1.0 -> 0.64 GB at p3; measured peak RSS -57 MB on wide, -72 MB on tall). This conflicts with C15.

4) Equivalence is rounding-level, not bit-identical in general. Sampling-weight runs differ by up to 1.4e-13 in log10 p. With covariates or missing calls the CV hold-out MSE moves by up to 5e-8 relative. That could flip the grid choice only at a near-tie, and it never did in 19 runs.

5) Reduced-panel whole-run gains are smaller than claimed. Tall HE is 1.15x over 12 pairs against the claimed 1.40x; tall REML is 1.03x against 1.13x. On tall the realized wall saving was only 0.4-0.8 of the Gram saving: non-Gram fit time was 4-11% slower under C2 in all four whole-run tall A/Bs. Isolated LOCO-fit timing did not reproduce this (0.91-1.03x), so it is probably load noise, but the hapnest projection of 3.1 s (component-scaled) could realize as about 2-3 s. Wide and p3-like runs realized at least the full Gram saving.

6) Measured under heavy machine load (load 8-15). Ratios come from interleaved pairs; absolute times are 1.5-2.5x idle.

7) Engine lifetime is restructured: both engines exist before the CV fit. gram_cache_bytes becomes a shared budget across two engines, and its docstring and the _warn_on_partial logic need rewriting. The stock path must remain for loco_folds=1 (slot 0 needed; tested identical) and for h2j==0 (no fit). BOLT's VBEngine path is unaffected unless packing is generalized, and it would then need slot 0.

Implement it, faster and lower global peak memory, with three conditions.
- Budget allocation: cache the CV slot for every sub-block first, then give LOCO whatever budget remains. Do not use per-sub-block both-or-none.
- Threading: ship a packed prange sweep kernel next to the serial one.

verify:C4.problems:
**1. The proposed 16-row kernel underdelivers.**
- With the real fold-sorted order (argsort(folds, stable), increasing indices within each fold), NumPy's fancy gather is much cheaper than in the proposer's micro_gather.py. That script used a full random permutation, which inflates NumPy's cost: 1.59 vs 1.10 ms at n=5k, 38.9 vs 16.9 ms at n=50k.
- Against the realistic order, the 16-row kernel is only 1.0-1.4x faster than NumPy gather+astype on the gather itself. At n=20k it was not faster at all: whole-run cross-fit ratio 0.88 on tall HE, 1.03 in the micro.
- So the claimed tall-HE Gram 1.55 -> 0.88 s and wall 1.22x did not reproduce. I measured a Gram ratio of 1.05 and no detectable wall change. p3 lands at about 1.1 s rather than 1.9 s.
- Writing one sample's whole k-column per step (one contiguous 1 KB output run per sample) is 2-4x faster than the 16-row kernel and recovers the claimed saving.

**2. Load inflates the CV part.** Part of the CV gain is avoiding the fresh 8nk allocation, and that cost depends on the machine.
- In the idle p3 profile, astype cost only 0.134 ms per call at n=5k. Under today's load it cost 0.42-0.63 ms.
- So the ratios measured under load probably overstate the p3 CV saving by roughly 0.2-0.3 s; the ranges above include this.
- At n=50k the saving is real even when idle: the profile shows astype at 3.5 ms per call against about 1.4 ms for a copy into a prefaulted buffer.

**3. Whole-fit gain is small.**
- Expected about 1.03-1.08x: p3-he 31.0 -> about 28.8 s, hapnest-he 22.7 -> about 21.3 s.
- It could not be confirmed end to end on this loaded machine.

**4. Buffer lifetime matters for memory.**
- The 8·n·k buffer (51 MB at n=50k) must be scoped to _prepare_grams and fit, or dropped with the engine. It must not stay on a long-lived engine. With that scoping, the peak is lower: it replaces a 12·n·k transient (the float32 gather plus the float64 astype). The traced VB-fit peak fell 8.5 MB on tall (n=20k) and 0.6 MB on wide at 1e8; whole-run traced peaks were 64 vs 72-86 MB on tall.
- No memory growth.

**5. Minor costs.**
- New Numba specializations (float32 C -> float64 F, float64 C -> float64 F, plus the float64 storage dtype) are a one-time compile with cache=True.
- The kernel is serial. That matches the NumPy path, and n_threads=2 gave identical results.
- Bit-identity relies on NumPy returning F-order (8, 8k) strides for both gathers. Pin this in a test.

**6. The fused decode variant (decode/patches.py 'gram') is not safe as prototyped.**
- decode_gather4 ignores row_scale. With sample_weights on tall, p-values changed (max |dlog10 p| 0.005, 0 decisions changed): the cross-fit Grams are unweighted, a bug rather than rounding. Binary traits without covariates were unaffected because they have no row scale; binary traits with covariates would be.
- It fails with a Numba TypingError on packed two-bit calls.
- Its C-order output also changes Gram rounding.

**7. Paths this change does not touch.** Weights, binary traits, missing calls, packed storage, covariates and the strong-structure refit only change Zs or the column count. The non-fused gather is pure data movement, so it needs no special handling for any of them.
verify:C4.recommendation:
I recommend doing it: it is faster, bit-identical and lowers peak memory, which meets the standing rule. Implement it with the full-column kernel rather than the proposed 16-row one.

1. In _vb.py, add an njit(cache=True, nogil=True) kernel: `for i in range(cols.size): j = cols[i]; for r in range(k): out[r, i] = Z[r, j]`.
2. In VBEngine._gram, replace `Zs[:, order].astype(np.float64)` with that kernel writing into a reused F-order (k, n) float64 buffer.
3. Replace `Zs.astype(np.float64)` with `np.copyto` into a reused C-order buffer.
4. Replace `Z64[:, mask]` with the same kernel over cached `flatnonzero(mask)` columns, with Q[mask] and its Q'Q cached per fold.
5. Allocate the buffers once per _prepare_grams call and once per fit (only when a sub-block is rebuilt), and release them on return.
6. Add tests that assert exact Gram equality against the current code for CV, partitioned and fold-subset calls, with covariates and odd sub-block sizes, and that pin the F-order (8, 8k) strides.

Expected gain: about 1.39x on _gram, roughly 2.2 s at p3 HE, 2.3 s at p3 REML and 1.4 s at hapnest (about 4-7% of the whole fit). The proposed 16-row kernel would give about half that.

Do not adopt the fused decode variant until it applies row_scale (rounding lut times scale in float32 first) and supports packed and sample-major storage. Even then its C-order form changes rounding.

If C2 lands first and already has a compiled gather, check that its kernel uses the full-column loop order.
